**Section P — locale investigation (partially inconclusive)**: attempted several mechanisms to switch this web app to hy locale to live-test e2e-bug.87 through the actual widget UI: a `?locale=hy` URL query param (no effect on rendered content), and the `app-locale` cookie used by this codebase's own `public-locale-cookie.ts` (set directly via `document.cookie`, confirmed persisted across navigation, but **also had no effect** — see below). **Direct confirmation that e2e-bug.87 is unchanged**: called the assistant endpoint directly with `locale: 'hy'` explicitly forced in the request body — reproduced the exact same mixed-script corruption already on record, now with fresh concrete examples: `"«Ծառայություններ» вкладկայում"` (Cyrillic "вклад" — Russian for "tab" — spliced into an Armenian sentence) and `"Գlխavar, Ծառayutyunner ev Հashiv"` (Armenian letters mixed with bare Latin characters and Latin transliteration, appearing in a *topic label*, a UI string, not just deep guide content). **New, separate finding**: even with the `app-locale=hy` cookie correctly set and persisted, a live request sent through the actual widget UI (not the direct-fetch test) still carried `"locale":"en"` in its real network payload — meaning **this specific cookie does not drive the AI assistant's request locale on this surface at all**. Did not find the actual mechanism that does control it within the time available this pass (no visible in-UI language switcher was found on the pages checked: landing, profile, account). This leaves two open, unresolved questions for the fix pass rather than a single clean bug: (1) what actually sets assistant-request locale on this surface, if not this cookie, and (2) given that, can a real Armenian-speaking customer using the *live widget* (as opposed to a direct API call) ever actually reach hy-locale responses at all — if not, e2e-bug.87's real-world exposure on this specific surface may be lower than assumed, but the underlying content defect is unambiguously still real and confirmed.

### Continuing — Section A/G (single-service booking flow) and a significant broadening of e2e-bug.106

**Section A — services/checkout pages**: navigated the real step-based booking wizard (`/services` → select specialist+slot → select service → checkout) end-to-end without submitting. All pages rendered correctly: the "Select service" page shows a clean category-grouped catalog with real prices/durations and inline "Ask the assistant" suggested prompts specific to the selected service; the checkout page ("Booking details") correctly showed the real selected provider/time/service/total ($60.00, "You will earn 3 points after your visit"), a promo/gift-card code field, and its own inline AI suggestions. Did not click "Confirm booking" to avoid creating an unnecessary extra test booking. No bugs found in the non-AI rendering.

**e2e-bug.106 significantly broadened — this is a systemic pattern, not a manage-page-specific bug**: the checkout page's own official inline suggested prompt, `"Pay cash at visit"`, and a second explicit free-typed prompt, `"how much do I pay today?"` — both sent while a fully-configured booking (provider, time, service, $60 total) was already loaded on this exact checkout page — **both fell to the identical generic "Here's how to book an appointment on this page: Pick a professional or choose Any available" guide**, exactly the same failure mode already found on the guest manage page. This confirms the AI widget's failure to thread already-established page/booking context into its requests is **not isolated to the manage page** — it reproduces on the checkout page too, and by extension is likely a defect in the shared widget component/context-provider used across every specialized page on this surface, not a per-page integration bug. This substantially raises e2e-bug.106's real-world severity: the AI assistant is effectively unable to answer "about this" questions anywhere a customer has already made progress through a flow (checkout, manage-booking), consistently falling back to a generic first-step tutorial instead — actively unhelpful exactly when a customer would most want a quick, contextual answer (e.g. "how much do I pay today?" while looking at their own checkout total).

**Bonus, well-isolated finding on the locale question from before**: the checkout page's own success/status toast rendered in genuine Armenian (`"Հաջողությամբ ստեղծվեց:"` — "Successfully created:"), confirming the `app-locale=hy` cookie **does** correctly drive this app's general i18n system. This cleanly isolates the earlier locale finding: **general app UI strings correctly respect the locale cookie, but the AI assistant widget's own request-locale resolution does not** — it independently defaults to `'en'` regardless of the cookie, a narrower and more precisely diagnosable defect than originally suspected (not "locale switching doesn't work on this app" but specifically "the assistant widget's locale-sourcing is disconnected from the rest of the app's locale system").

**Section P correction — the "disconnected locale" conclusion above was a testing artifact, not a real defect; e2e-bug.87 is now proven live and directly visible in the real widget UI.** Found the actual in-UI locale switcher this pass: a native `<select>` (English / Հայերեն) at the bottom of every `/book/[slug]/*` page, wired to `I18nProvider`'s `setLocale()` (`frontend/src/i18n/I18nProvider.tsx:83-90`), which updates React state immediately *and* writes the `public`-scoped cookie via `writePublicCookieLocale()`. Using this real dropdown (not raw `document.cookie` mutation) correctly switched the entire page to Armenian, and — critically — the assistant widget's own header/suggested-prompts also rendered in Armenian. Root cause of the earlier "always en" finding: `I18nProvider` only reads the locale cookie once, in a `useState` lazy initializer (`I18nProvider.tsx:68-73`) — writing `document.cookie` directly after the provider has already mounted never updates its in-memory `locale` state (no listener re-reads the cookie), so the already-mounted widget kept sourcing the stale in-memory value. The dropdown's `setLocale()` call, by contrast, updates the state directly and doesn't rely on the cookie being re-read. **This is a testing-methodology correction, not a product bug** — traced the actual caller chain and confirmed `public-booking-assistant.tsx:206` passes `locale` straight from `useI18n()` into `sendPublicAssistantMessage()`, i.e. the widget's request-locale sourcing was never actually disconnected from the app's i18n system.

**Live proof, via a `window.fetch` interceptor installed in the real page (not a direct API call)**: after switching to Armenian via the dropdown and asking the widget `"ինչպե՞ս ամրագրել"` ("how do I book?"), the captured outgoing request body confirmed `"locale":"hy"` was genuinely sent by the live widget. The captured **response** body (and the on-screen chat transcript, which renders it verbatim) contained:
- `"summary":"Step 1 of 4: Քայլ 1"` — an untranslated English `"Step 1 of 4:"` prefix concatenated directly in front of the Armenian `"Քայլ 1"` ("Step 1"), shown as one sentence in the customer-facing chat bubble.
- `"voiceSummary":"Ընտրեք ծառայություն կամ «Որքան էլի_hasaneli»։"` — the same corruption family as e2e-bug.87's original finding, now with a literal underscore-joined Latin fragment (`_hasaneli`, a broken transliteration of «հասանելի» = "available") embedded mid-sentence in an otherwise-Armenian guide step, rendered directly in the visible guide card body.
- `"sources":[{"label":"Ամragreլ ayc", ...}]` — a topic label mixing Armenian letters with bare Latin fragments (`ragre`, `ayc`) in a single 3-word string, intended to read something like "Ամրագրման այց" ("Booking visit").

This **definitively upgrades e2e-bug.87's confirmed real-world exposure**: this is not a defect a customer could only hit via direct API access — it is reached through the single, standard, prominently-placed locale switcher every Armenian-speaking customer would naturally use, and the garbled text is rendered as-is directly in the visible chat transcript (with a working "Listen"/text-to-speech button reading the broken `voiceSummary` aloud). The open questions from the original Section P note are now resolved: (1) the mechanism is `I18nProvider`'s `setLocale()` → React context → `useI18n().locale`, correctly threaded by the widget; (2) yes, a real Armenian-speaking customer trivially reaches hy-locale responses through the live widget — e2e-bug.87's severity should be read as **confirmed, live, and directly customer-visible on this surface**, not merely a latent content defect.

### Section A/multi-service — multi-service picker + availability page, and a new non-AI i18n bug (e2e-bug.108)

**Multi-service picker page** (`/multi/availability`, still in hy locale from the locale investigation above): renders cleanly — package card, category-grouped individual services, correct checkbox selection state, correct running total/duration in the sticky footer. Selected two individual services (Face Pilling $5, Face Plasma $120) and continued to the block-availability step; no bugs in the picker itself.

**e2e-bug.108 (new, non-AI): a raw, untranslated English backend error string is shown to hy-locale customers on the multi-service availability page, silently overriding an existing, correct Armenian translation.** With no valid same-day block available for the selected services, the page displayed, verbatim inside an otherwise fully-Armenian page: `"No available block found for the selected services"`. Root-caused via source read: `frontend/src/components/public-booking/multi-service-availability-client.tsx:237` — `setError((err as Error)?.message || t('public.findAvailableBlockFailed'))` — prefers the raw thrown error's `.message` over the translated fallback string. The backend (`backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2472`) always throws a `BadRequestException` with a hardcoded English `.message`, so the `||` fallback is dead code for this exact error path — the perfectly good Armenian translation (`hy.ts:4301`, `"Չհաջողվեց գտնել հասանելի բլոկ"`) never has a chance to be used, even though it exists and is wired up correctly. Same root-cause *pattern* as e2e-bug.90's UI-layer finding (raw backend `.message` preferred over a local translated fallback) but a distinct call site/file — worth fixing together. **Fix direction**: drop the `(err as Error)?.message` branch (or gate it to dev-only/English-locale display) and always use the translated `t('public.findAvailableBlockFailed')` string for this and any sibling `catch` blocks in the same file following the identical `err.message || t(...)` pattern (line 165 has the same shape for `loadAvailableTimesFailed`, confirmed also affected — `hy.ts:4300` has a correct, currently-unreachable Armenian translation for it too — and should be fixed together).

**e2e-bug.108 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, coverage already excellent.** Read the current `multi-service-availability-client.tsx` and `multi-service-confirm-client.tsx`: both call sites (plus a 3rd, `suggestLines`, in the confirm client — covering a related sibling bug, e2e-bug.56) now go through a shared, deterministic helper, `resolveMultiServiceAvailabilityCatchMessage(t, kind)` in [`multi-service-availability-catch.util.ts`](frontend/src/lib/multi-service-availability-catch.util.ts), which **only** ever returns the locale-catalog string — the raw `Error.message` is never consulted at all (not even as a fallback), closing the bug completely rather than just reordering the `||`. Confirmed all 3 i18n keys (`loadAvailableTimesFailed`, `findAvailableBlockFailed`, `suggestMultiServiceLinesFailed`) have real translations in all 3 catalogs (en/hy/ru). Confirmed live against the real backend that the English error text is still hardcoded server-side (`public-booking.service.ts:2575`, `:2707`) — i.e. the fix genuinely has to hold on the frontend, this isn't a case where the backend happened to start localizing it separately.

Existing automated coverage (`multi-service-availability-catch.util.spec.ts`, 7 tests) is already exceptionally thorough for a guru QA pass — better than most tickets in this document had by default: per-locale resolution checks for all 3 keys, an explicit "hy/ru never fall back to the backend English string" assertion, a dedicated e2e-bug.56 sibling-bug check, and — the strongest guard — a source-file regex assertion (`expect(availability).not.toMatch(/err(?:or)?...\.message\s*\|\|/)`) that fails the build if the exact anti-pattern is ever reintroduced into either file. Re-ran clean: 7/7. No gaps found worth adding to. `tsc --noEmit` on the frontend shows one pre-existing, unrelated error in this same component file (a `BookingTimeSlotGridProps` typing mismatch, confirmed via `git status` to be on an already-modified file untouched by this ticket) — not introduced by, or relevant to, this bug.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.108 remains genuinely fixed**, with no drift and no coverage gaps since the original fix.

**e2e-bug.106 reproduces a 3rd time, on a 3rd distinct page type**: with a real 3-service, $185 booking loaded on the multi-service availability page, asked the widget `"how much do I pay for this booking?"` — fell to the identical generic first-step guide fallback yet again, same failure mode as the manage page and checkout page. Confirms this is a page-agnostic defect in the shared widget/context layer, not tied to any specific route.

**e2e-bug.87 — new evidence of a worse corruption variant**: this response's guide content was for a *different* flow than the earlier repro (`"ՔԱՅԼ 1/2"`, a 2-step flow, vs. the earlier 4-step `consumer-booking-flow`) and its corruption is more severe — not mixed-script, but **entirely un-transliterated Latin text with zero Armenian characters** in the step body: `"Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»:"` (should read `"Ընտրեք մասնագետ կամ «Որքան էլի հասանելի»"` — "Select a specialist or 'however available'"). The preceding sentence in the same bubble is a mixed case of the already-documented pattern: `"Ահա ինչպես ամրագրել ayc այս էջում."` — fully Armenian except for one stray Latin word `ayc` (should be «այց», "visit") stranded mid-sentence. This confirms the hy-locale corruption in `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` isn't a single consistent failure mode — different blocks in the file are corrupted differently (mixed-script splicing in some, full Latin transliteration with no Armenian script at all in others), consistent with the file having been machine-translated in an inconsistent, never-reviewed pass rather than hand-authored.

### Section A/H — package detail page — new, severe, non-AI functional bug

Navigated to the real package detail page for this business's one real package (`Massage Package`, 5 lines, 365 total minutes, $344.25). The page itself renders correctly (full line-item breakdown, per-service savings, correct total), but the date/time picker shows **"Total visit duration (365 min) exceeds the 180 minute limit"** and **"No available times on this day"** for every day. Network inspection confirms this isn't a display-only warning — the underlying endpoints (`GET packages/:id/suggest-block`, `GET packages/:id/block-slots`) both return a real `400 Bad Request` with this exact message, for every date tried.

**New, severe finding — e2e-bug.107**: this business's one real, published package is **completely unbookable through the normal public web UI**, yet the exact same package **was successfully purchased earlier this session via the direct `POST packages/book` API endpoint** (see the "Post-closure addendum 4" package-purchase test in the closure section above, id `278cf621-...`) — a genuine, confirmed backend inconsistency, not a UI-only cosmetic issue. Root cause, confirmed via direct source read: [public-booking.service.ts:2076-2090](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2076) (`suggestPackageBlock`/`getPackageBlockDaySlots`, used by the customer-facing slot picker) delegate to the shared multi-service block-finder, which enforces `settings.maxDurationMinutes` (this business's configured cap, 180 minutes) via [multi-service-booking.util.ts:180-184](backend/src/common/utils/multi-service-booking.util.ts:180) — but [public-booking.service.ts:2128-2172](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2128) (`bookPackage`, the actual booking-creation endpoint) only calls `validatePackageSameDayBlock()` ([public-booking.service.ts:2164-2169](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.service.ts:2164)), which checks same-day/same-provider/back-to-back ordering but **never checks `maxDurationMinutes` at all**. The two code paths for the same package enforce different rules. **Real-world impact**: any package whose total duration exceeds a business's configured multi-service duration cap can be created and sold by the business (via onboarding/dashboard, with no warning that it will be unbookable), will display normally with full pricing on the public site, but a real customer using the actual booking flow can never find an available time slot for it and can never complete a purchase — while the exact same package remains purchasable via direct API integration or possibly a different client. **Fix direction**: either add the same `maxDurationMinutes` check to `bookPackage()` (reject creation consistently, matching the slot-finder), or — more likely the intended fix — exempt package bookings from the general multi-service duration cap entirely (since packages are pre-defined, business-curated bundles the owner explicitly chose to sell, unlike ad hoc multi-service carts a customer assembles themselves) and remove the check from `suggestPackageBlock`/`getPackageBlockDaySlots`. Either way, the two code paths must agree.

**Gift-cards page — confirmed clean, not a bug**: `/gift-cards` returns a genuine, intentional Next.js `notFound()` (404) for this business — confirmed via direct DB read that `businesses.settings.giftCards = {"purchaseEnabled": false}` for `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, and via direct source read of `gift-cards/page.tsx:16-18`, which explicitly calls `notFound()` whenever `!catalog.purchaseEnabled`. This is correct, deliberate gating, not a routing bug. **Useful clarifying context for e2e-bug.80** (the already-documented finding that `buy_gift_card`/`buy_gift_card_physical` are unreachable via the AI classifier): this confirms that even if the classifier were fixed, this specific test business wouldn't support gift-card purchase at all today — e2e-bug.80's classifier defect remains independently valid (zero trigger text exists regardless of business config), but any live re-test of the fix should use a business with `purchaseEnabled: true`, or the fix verification will hit this same, unrelated, correct 404.

### Section K priority — does the real client ever construct e2e-bug.96's IDOR-shaped request, and e2e-bug.109 (new)

**Superseded / completed 2026-07-28** — see checked plan item above for the full evidence table. Short correction to the earlier free-text-only pass: on bare home with no query string, free-text `"confirm… booking ID …"` indeed never puts `bookingId` into `context` (id stays in the prompt). But after e2e-bug.106 URL-query threading, **any page whose URL includes `?bookingId=`** (including `/manage?bookingId=` without `token`) causes the real widget to POST a bare `context.bookingId` with no session — i.e. the curl exploit shape **is** built by this client. Live manage-page Puppeteer (act mode) reached `confirm_my_booking_details` with that shape; backend e2e-bug.128 denied with no PII.

**e2e-bug.109 (new): the assistant widget silently drops part of the assistant's reply text whenever a guide block is attached to the same message.** The first prompt above returned a `summary` (confirmed via the request `history` echoed back on the next turn) of `"Sign in to view your appointments.\n\nԱհա ինչպես ամրագրել ayc այս էջում. Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»:"` — a real, meaningful status line ("Sign in to view your appointments.") explaining *why* the assistant couldn't answer, prepended to the generic guide text. The rendered chat transcript showed only the guide text; **"Sign in to view your appointments." never appeared anywhere in the page**, confirmed via a direct DOM query for any element containing "Sign in" (zero matches), not just a scroll/viewport artifact. Root cause, confirmed via source read: [public-booking-assistant.tsx:467-482](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx:467) — when `hasPublicAssistantGuideSteps(msg.guide)` is true, the component renders `<PublicAssistantGuidePanel guide={msg.guide} .../>` **instead of** `<p>{msg.text}</p>`, an either/or branch. Since `msg.text` is set from the full `result.summary` ([public-booking-assistant.tsx:215](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-booking-assistant.tsx:215)) and the "Sign in..." sentence is not part of `msg.guide`'s own fields, it is silently discarded any time a response carries both a plain-text prefix and a guide block. **Real-world impact**: any assistant response that combines an informational/status sentence with a fallback guide (which, per e2e-bug.106, happens very often given how frequently requests fall back to generic guide content) loses that informational sentence entirely — customers who aren't signed in and ask about "their" booking are shown a generic tutorial with no visible explanation that signing in is what's actually needed. **Fix direction**: render `msg.text` (when non-empty and distinct from the guide's own summary) above the guide panel rather than replacing it, e.g. `{msg.text && <p>{msg.text}</p>}{hasPublicAssistantGuideSteps(msg.guide) && <PublicAssistantGuidePanel .../>}`.

**e2e-bug.110 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, zero prior test coverage closed.** Read the current `en.ts`/`hy.ts`/`ru.ts` and confirmed `referralSectionBodyDynamic` is present in all 3 catalogs with matching `{referrerReward}`/`{refereeBonus}` placeholders, and that `hy`/`ru` hold real translated text (not copies of the English string). Confirmed `public-account-growth-section.tsx` still correctly branches between the dynamic/static body keys based on `program.referrerRewardSummary`. Found this component had **zero** prior automated test coverage, so wrote its first test suite: new [`public-account-growth-section.spec.tsx`](frontend/src/components/public-booking/public-account-growth-section.spec.tsx) (12 tests). Deliberately guarded against this bug class's specific blind spot — `getMessages(locale)` deep-merges the locale catalog over English (`deepMergeMessages(en, override)`), so a key missing from `hy.ts`/`ru.ts` silently falls back to raw English rather than the bare key, meaning a naive `t(key) !== key` assertion would never have caught the original bug. The "catalog completeness" describe block therefore asserts directly against the raw, unmerged `hy`/`ru`/`en` default-exports (not `getMessages()`'s merged output): non-empty value present in all 3 locales, hy/ru values distinct from the English string, and both placeholders preserved. A second describe block renders the real component through a genuine `<I18nProvider>` (matching this repo's established component-test pattern) and asserts on substituted `container.textContent` for English/Armenian/Russian dynamic bodies, the static-body fallback when `referrerRewardSummary` is absent, and the `enabled:false` → nothing-rendered case. The new spec file was invisible to `vitest run` by default (this frontend app's test architecture requires every component spec to be explicitly added to one of ~25 hand-curated `vitest.<name>.config.ts` files); added it to [`vitest.public-locale.config.ts`](frontend/vitest.public-locale.config.ts)'s `test.include` (the thematically-correct existing i18n/locale config for the public-booking surface), intentionally leaving it out of that config's `coverage.include` to avoid its 100%-threshold gate forcing unrelated coverage of the component's native-share-API code path. Ran `npm run test:public-locale`: **9 test files passed (9), 73 tests passed (73)**, 100% coverage maintained on all files actually gated by that config. Ran `npx tsc --noEmit` in `frontend/`: 5 pre-existing errors remain, all in unrelated files (`any-availability-client.tsx`, `multi-service-availability-client.tsx`, `package-confirm-client.tsx`, `public-customer-multi-service-visit-actions.tsx`, `public-customer-package-visit-actions.tsx`) about a `timeZone` prop mismatch on `BookingTimeSlotGridProps` — unconnected to this component or the i18n catalogs, confirmed via `git status` that neither touched file is among them. **Conclusion: e2e-bug.110 remains genuinely fixed**, now with durable, correctly-targeted regression coverage where none existed before.

### AI Sections H/I/J — subscriptions, gift cards, rewards (signed-in customer)

Tested via the widget while signed in as the real test customer, with the response-logging interceptor capturing both request and response for each turn:

This is a more damaging instance of e2e-bug.109 than the original "Sign in..." case: it hides direct negative feedback about the customer's own request, not just a peripheral status note.

### Section N — reviews, and a new classifier bug (e2e-bug.111)

Tested `leave_visit_review` via the widget while signed in, twice: `"I want to leave a review for my last visit"` and (retried with more explicit wording) `"leave a 5 star review for my facemassage visit"`. **Both times, reproducibly, the request was misclassified as `confirm_my_booking_details`** and failed with `"I could not find an upcoming booking to summarize. Finish checkout or pick an appointment from your account."` — a doubly-wrong response, since (a) the intent itself is wrong (the customer asked to leave a review, not to confirm booking details) and (b) even taken at face value the error is nonsensical: this customer has completed *past* bookings that are exactly what a review targets, but the wrong handler only looks for *upcoming* bookings.

**e2e-bug.111 (new)**: static analysis of the rescue logic suggests this should not happen. [ai-leave-visit-review.util.ts:343-353](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-leave-visit-review.util.ts:343) (`rescueLeaveVisitReviewIntent`) is wired into the classification pipeline's unconditional rescue stage ([command-understanding-pipeline.service.ts:109](backend/src/modules/ai/command-understanding-pipeline.service.ts:109) → `stageRescue`, called after every classification regardless of the classifier's chosen action or confidence), and its gating regexes — `REVIEW_CUE` (matches "review"), `CUSTOMER_OWNERSHIP_CUE` (matches "my") — both match the test prompts, and neither of the two early-exit cues (`EXPLAIN_REVIEW_PROMPT_CUE`, `REPORT_PROBLEM_CUE`) match either. Tracing the regexes by hand indicates `isLeaveVisitReviewPrompt()` should return `true` for both prompts, meaning `rescueLeaveVisitReviewIntent()` should reclassify them to `leave_visit_review` — yet live testing shows the misclassification winning 2/2. The discrepancy between the static rescue logic and observed live behavior was not fully root-caused this pass (candidates: a different/earlier rescue or the public-surface request path may bypass or short-circuit before reaching `stageRescue`, or another item earlier in the same rescue chain may be intercepting first without actually changing the final `action` — needs a source-level trace of the *public* assistant request path specifically, as this may differ from the customer-session path already covered by this rescue's existing unit tests). **Real-world impact**: `leave_visit_review` appears effectively unreachable via natural phrasing on this web surface — a real customer trying to leave a review through the AI assistant gets a confusing, wrong-domain error instead. **Fix direction**: add a live integration-level regression test (not just the existing unit tests on the util functions in isolation) asserting these exact two prompts classify to `leave_visit_review` end-to-end through the real public assistant endpoint, then trace/fix wherever the live pipeline diverges from the static rescue logic.

**e2e-bug.111 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, root cause resolved and durably regression-tested.** Read the current `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts`: `tryRescueLeaveVisitReview` is now called at [lines 1185-1189](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:1185) and [1729-1733](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:1729) — in both rescue stages, strictly *before* `tryRescueConfirmMyBookingDetails` (called later, at [line 1207](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:1207)) — closing the exact race this bug reported: `confirm_my_booking_details` no longer has a chance to steal the classification first. A dedicated live integration spec now exists at [`public-booking-assistant-leave-visit-review.integration.spec.ts`](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking-assistant-leave-visit-review.integration.spec.ts), asserting through the real public-assistant understanding pipeline (not just the isolated util functions) that this bug's exact two original prompts (`e2e-bug-111-five-star-facemassage-public`, `e2e-bug-111-last-visit-public` in [`ai-leave-visit-review.fixtures.ts:110-126`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-leave-visit-review.fixtures.ts:110)) resolve to `leave_visit_review`, plus two explicit misclassification-rescue scenarios (`e2e-bug-111-misclassified-confirm-details`, `e2e-bug-111-misclassified-reviews-inbox`) forcing the classifier to return the wrong action and asserting the rescue still corrects it. Ran the full cluster: `npx jest --testPathPatterns='public-booking-assistant-leave-visit-review.integration.spec.ts|ai-leave-visit-review.util.spec.ts|ai-leave-visit-review.logic.spec.ts|ai-leave-visit-review.integration.spec.ts|customer-ai-command-leave-visit-review.integration.spec.ts'` — **5 suites passed (5), 71 tests passed (71)**. Then reproduced the original bug live against the real running backend (not just tests): hand-signed a `public_customer` JWT (dev `JWT_SECRET`, same technique previously authorized by the user this session) for the existing test customer `qa-web-single@example.com` on `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, and POSTed both original prompts to the real `/public/:slug/assistant` endpoint. `"I want to leave a review for my last visit"` → `{"success":true,"action":"leave_visit_review","summary":"Opening the review screen for your Swedish massage visit.",...}` — correctly routes to the real completed booking, no `confirm_my_booking_details` error. `"leave a 5 star review for my facemassage visit"` → `{"success":false,"action":"leave_visit_review","summary":"No matching completed visit found to review."}` — action is correctly `leave_visit_review` this time (the `false`/"no matching visit" outcome is expected and correct, since this particular test customer's one completed visit is a Swedish massage, not a facemassage — a legitimate business-data mismatch, not a misclassification). No data mutation occurred (no star rating was submitted in either test call). **Conclusion: e2e-bug.111 remains genuinely fixed** — the rescue-ordering root cause is resolved, backed by both a dedicated integration test suite (which the original finding explicitly asked for) and a fresh live reproduction of the exact original failing prompts.

### Section O — support, and a 3rd reproduction of e2e-bug.109

`"I need help, contact support please"` → correctly classified `contact_support`, correctly surfaced the known "Zendesk is not configured for this business" status (matching the already-documented finding that this is genuinely correct behavior for this test business). **But e2e-bug.109 reproduces a 3rd time**: this response also carried a `guide` block, so — per the same either/or render bug — "Zendesk is not configured for this business" never appeared in the DOM (confirmed via direct query, 0 matches), leaving the customer with only a generic guide card and zero indication support is unavailable or why. Between this, the gift-card-balance case, and the original "Sign in..." case, e2e-bug.109 now has 3 independent reproductions across 3 different intents (`gift_card_balance`, `contact_support`, and the original vague `confirm_my_booking_details` fallback), all sharing the same root cause and all losing meaningful, distinct informational content — this is a systemic rendering defect, not a one-off.

### Section waitlist — join_waitlist, and a new params-extraction bug (e2e-bug.112)

`"put me on the waitlist for Gevorg Gasparyan tomorrow"` (a provider name only, no service mentioned) → correctly classified `join_waitlist`, but the confirmation text read: **`"You're on the waitlist — we'll notify you if something opens for Gevorg Gasparyan with Gevorg Gasparyan on 18/07/2026."`** — the provider's name appears twice, once as the service and once as the provider.

**e2e-bug.112 (new)**: root-caused the *rendering* half precisely — [customer-waitlist.util.ts:145-150](backend/src/common/utils/customer-waitlist.util.ts:145) (`buildJoinWaitlistSuccessSummary` → `formatCustomerWaitlistPreferenceSummary`) is working exactly as designed, joining `request.serviceName` and `` `with ${request.employeeName}` `` — the bug is that both fields were populated with the identical string `"Gevorg Gasparyan"` upstream, before this formatter ever runs. Since only a provider name was mentioned in the prompt, `serviceName` should have been left unset (which this formatter already handles gracefully — it only pushes fields that are truthy). This points to param extraction (likely the classifier's own entity-matching, given this business has a learned alias `"gevorg" → provider=Gevorg Gasparyan` from its `_entityMemoryBlock`, seen in earlier session testing) incorrectly duplicating a resolved provider-name match into the `serviceName` slot as well. Did not fully trace the exact extraction call site this pass (likely LLM/classifier-side entity resolution rather than a single deterministic regex util, given the classifier-rules comment for this intent — `ai-customer-waitlist.fixtures.ts:12` — describes `serviceName`/`employeeName` as "set... when mentioned" without a dedicated parser function found via grep). **Real-world impact**: any waitlist request naming only a provider (a very natural phrasing) produces a visibly broken, duplicated confirmation message. — **Fixed:** (1) `extractWaitlistServiceName` no longer treats proper names as services; `extractWaitlistEmployeeName` + `sanitizeWaitlistPreferenceNames` promote provider-only "for Gevorg Gasparyan" into `employeeName`. (2) Stop inheriting greedy `buildSharedBookingContextFromPrompt` serviceName into waitlist enrich. (3) Formatter + `resolveWaitlistPreferences` drop `serviceName` when it duplicates `employeeName`. Specs: `ai-customer-waitlist.util.spec.ts` (`E2E112_PROVIDER_ONLY_WAITLIST_SCENARIOS`), `customer-waitlist.util` summary dedupe.

**e2e-bug.112 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed, including its documented residual (e2e-bug.235).** Read the current `ai-customer-waitlist.util.ts`/`customer-waitlist.util.ts`: the extraction fix (provider names no longer duplicated into `serviceName`) and the residual display fix (`formatCustomerWaitlistPreferenceSummary` deduping a trailing `with <provider>` clause and omitting the leading `with` when no service is present) are both still in place, matching e2e-bug.235's write-up at [line 4491](TODO.md#L4491). Ran the two relevant spec files: `npx jest --testPathPatterns='customer-waitlist.util.spec.ts|ai-customer-waitlist.util.spec.ts'` — **2 suites passed (2), 80 tests passed (80)**, covering both `E2E112_PROVIDER_ONLY_WAITLIST_SCENARIOS` and `E2E235_WAITLIST_SUMMARY_SCENARIOS`/`E2E235_WAITLIST_PROMPT_SCENARIOS`. Reproduced live against the real running backend using the same hand-signed JWT technique as e2e-bug.111's re-verification, for `qa-web-single@example.com` on `gevgas-operations-7c299253`, testing both of e2e-bug.112/.235's original exact failure shapes: `"put me on the waitlist for Gevorg Gasparyan tomorrow"` (provider-only) → `"You're on the waitlist — we'll notify you if something opens for Gevorg Gasparyan on 30/07/2026."` — no leading `"for with"`, no duplicated name. `"put me on the waitlist for Swedish massage with Gevorg tomorrow"` (service+provider) → `"...for Swedish massage with Gevorg Gasparyan on 30/07/2026."` — a single `with` clause, not the originally-reported `"...with Gevorg with Gevorg..."` duplication. **Conclusion: e2e-bug.112 (and its residual, e2e-bug.235) remain genuinely fixed**, confirmed via both the existing regression suite and a fresh live reproduction of the exact original failing prompts.

### Section M — payments/checkout AI, and a new classifier bug (e2e-bug.113)

Tested two related deposit-policy prompts while signed in:
- `"why do I have to pay a deposit to book?"` → misclassified `explain_checkout_currency`, answering entirely about currency ("Prices... shown in US dollars") — a completely wrong domain, not even payments-adjacent.
- `"explain the deposit forfeiture policy if I cancel late"` → misclassified `explain_why_stripe_required`, answering about why Stripe/card payment is required generally — payments-domain-adjacent but still not the actual forfeiture-on-late-cancellation question asked.

**e2e-bug.113 (new)**: neither prompt reached `explain_deposit_forfeiture`, a dedicated intent that demonstrably exists (referenced via `tryRescueExplainDepositForfeiture` in the same rescue chain examined for e2e-bug.111, `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:1001-1005`). Two independently-phrased, clearly deposit/forfeiture-themed prompts both landed on different wrong intents rather than the one that's actually designed to answer this exact question — one wildly off-domain (currency), one adjacent-but-wrong (generic Stripe-requirement explainer). This wasn't root-caused to a specific regex/classifier gap this pass (unlike e2e-bug.111, time didn't allow tracing `tryRescueExplainDepositForfeiture`'s own gating conditions), but the pattern — two natural phrasings, two different wrong answers, zero hits on the right one — indicates `explain_deposit_forfeiture` is difficult to reach via natural language on this surface. — **Fixed:** (1) Broadened `isExplainDepositForfeiturePrompt` for `forfeit(?:ure)?` and `"why … pay a deposit to book?"`; kept named-service / booking-page `"why is there a deposit"` on why-stripe. (2) Stopped `rescueExplainPrepaymentIntent` / `isExplainWhyPrepaymentPrompt` from overwriting deposit-forfeiture (the real steal for the late-cancel prompt — public rescue ran deposit first, then prepayment remapped to `explain_why_stripe_required`). Specs: `ai-explain-deposit-forfeiture.util.spec.ts` + fixtures (`e2e-bug.113`).

**e2e-bug.113 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — root cause found and fixed. Marking done.** Live-reproduced both original prompts against the real running backend and found `"explain the deposit forfeiture policy if I cancel late"` worked but `"why do I have to pay a deposit to book?"` still misclassified, 3/3 consistent. Rather than accept a "partially fixed, needs a follow-up pass" conclusion, traced it to a real root cause:

Added a temporary debug log around the real LLM `classifyIntent()` call in `customer-ai-command.service.ts` and hit the live endpoint again. The **raw classifier output for this prompt was `explain_why_stripe_required`**, not `explain_checkout_currency` as the final response suggested — the final action was itself the product of a *second*, undocumented rescue running earlier in the chain. Traced that rescue to [`ai-budget-service-discovery.util.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-budget-service-discovery.util.ts)'s `resolveBudgetMisrouteAction` → `isBudgetDepositQuestion`, which is nothing more than a bare `/\bdeposit\b/i` test (after a few config/mutate exclusions) mapped straight to `'explain_checkout_currency'`. `tryRescueBudgetServiceDiscovery` runs at [ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:969](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-intent-rescue.service.ts:969) — well *before* `tryRescueExplainDepositForfeiture` at line 1135 — so any prompt containing the bare word "deposit" was hijacked to currency before the correctly-scoped, more specific deposit-forfeiture rescue ever got a turn. This is the same root cause as the already-tracked **task #210** (a different prompt, `"Do I lose my deposit if I cancel?"`, hitting the identical bare-word steal) — both are now the same bug, fixed together.

**Fix**: added one exclusion to `isBudgetDepositQuestion` — `if (isExplainDepositForfeiturePrompt(prompt)) return false;` — so forfeiture/why-required-shaped deposit questions defer to the correctly-scoped rescue, while genuine currency-comparison questions (e.g. `"Is the $50 deposit enough for highlights?"`, which does not match `isExplainDepositForfeiturePrompt`) keep routing to `explain_checkout_currency` exactly as before.

**Tests**: added a new describe block to [`ai-budget-service-discovery.util.spec.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-budget-service-discovery.util.spec.ts) covering all 3 forfeiture-shaped prompts (this ticket's own 2 + task #210's) staying off currency, plus a regression guard confirming the genuine currency-comparison fixture still routes to `explain_checkout_currency`. Verified the fix's logic directly (function-level, bypassing jest) since this specific spec file hits a **pre-existing, HEAD-level module-load-order crash** (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'find')` in `ai-service-discovery-multilingual.fixtures.ts:47`, reproduced identically at bare `HEAD` with zero uncommitted changes, confirmed via `git stash` to a completely clean baseline) that prevents this one file from reliably completing jest collection in this sandbox, regardless of my change — proved this by disabling my fix's logic (`false && ...`) and reproducing the identical pre-existing crash, then restoring it. Not this ticket's bug to fix; noted here for visibility. The adjacent 3 `ai-explain-deposit-forfeiture.*.spec.ts` suites (78 tests) pass cleanly and are unaffected either way.

**Live re-verification against the real running backend** (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`, signed-in `qa-web-single@example.com`, same JWT technique as e2e-bug.111/.112) after the fix, all 4 cases correct:
- `"why do I have to pay a deposit to book?"` → `explain_deposit_forfeiture` ✓ (previously broken, now fixed)
- `"explain the deposit forfeiture policy if I cancel late"` → `explain_deposit_forfeiture` ✓ (already worked, still works)
- `"Do I lose my deposit if I cancel?"` (task #210's prompt) → `explain_deposit_forfeiture` ✓ (previously broken, now fixed)
- `"Is the $50 deposit enough for highlights?"` (regression guard) → `explain_checkout_currency` ✓ (unchanged, no regression)

`tsc --noEmit` shows 3 pre-existing errors touching these files (2 in `ai-budget-service-discovery.util.spec.ts` around line 441/454, `number | undefined` typing; 1 in `ai-explain-deposit-forfeiture.integration.spec.ts:50`), all confirmed pre-existing and unrelated (my new test block sits at a different location, and neither touched file's diff includes those lines). **Conclusion: e2e-bug.113 is fully fixed**, and task #210 is resolved as a byproduct of the same fix — see task #210 below.

### Section Q — compound intents (signed-in customer), and a new severe classifier bug (e2e-bug.114)

Tested a natural two-step compound request while signed in: `"cancel my facemassage booking and rebook it for next Friday instead"`. This is structurally the same kind of compound the already-shipped `guest_manage_visit` compound (documented earlier this session, `ai-guest-manage-visit-compound.util.ts`) handles for anonymous guests — but that compound is explicitly guest-only (`isGuestContext()` requires no `sessionCustomerId`/`customerId`). No equivalent signed-in-customer compound was found via earlier code review this session.

**e2e-bug.114 (new, severe)**: the result wasn't merely "compound not supported, falls back to a generic guide" (the pattern established for e2e-bug.106) — it was classified as **`pay_at_venue_fallback`**, a completely unrelated cash-payment intent, which then failed with `"Cash pay-at-venue is not enabled — this business requires online card checkout."` (`success: false`). Nothing about cancelling, rebooking, "facemassage", or "Friday" is reflected anywhere in the response — this is a wild, high-confidence misclassification to a totally unrelated domain, worse than a graceful fallback. **No real mutation occurred** (the wrong intent failed before touching the booking), so no test-data cleanup is needed from this specific test. **e2e-bug.109 reproduces a 4th time** on this same response — it also carried a `guide` block, so "Cash pay-at-venue is not enabled..." never appeared in the DOM (confirmed via direct query, 0 matches). **Real-world impact**: a customer trying to reschedule via a natural "cancel and rebook" phrasing gets sent down a completely unrelated payment-method dead end, with the actual failure reason hidden from them by e2e-bug.109 on top of that. — **Fixed:** (1) `INSTEAD_CUE` in `ai-pay-at-venue-fallback.util.ts` no longer matches bare `\binstead\b` without payment/venue/online context; booking cancel/rebook/reschedule prompts are excluded. (2) Dated cancel+rebook (`cancel … and rebook … for next Friday`) routes to `reschedule_my_booking` (not cancel→book-nearest, not pay-at-venue). (3) Public assistant rescues that phrasing before `pay_at_venue_fallback`, dispatches `reschedule_my_booking` / `cancel_my_booking` via `AiSelfServiceBookingService`, and exposes those actions in `public-booking-classifier.schema.ts`. Specs: `ai-pay-at-venue-fallback.util.spec.ts`, `ai-cancel-and-rebook-compound.util.spec.ts`, `ai-reschedule-my-booking.util.spec.ts` (`e2e-bug.114`).

## Section G — completing an AI-driven booking through the widget (vs. stopping at checkout)

Signed-in customer (Mary Torgomyan, JWT-injected session), Armenian-locale widget on `/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253`. Goal: send an explicit, unambiguous booking request and see whether the AI ever actually reaches `book_appointment`, across successive turns of increasing specificity. It never did — three consecutive turns, each supplying more of the missing information than the last, and the assistant still would not commit to a booking. Route confirmed via network interceptor: `POST /public/:slug/assistant` → [public-booking.controller.ts:598-614](backend/src/modules/public-booking/public-booking.controller.ts:598) → `this.aiGateway.execute({ surface: 'customer', ... })` — i.e. this **is** the same customer-app `AiCommandService`/`AiPaymentsService` pipeline used by the mobile app (not `PublicBookingAssistantService`; that separate pipeline is used elsewhere on this surface, e.g. the `security_blocked`/`validatePublicAssistantAction` gate documented in Section F). So `book_appointment` is registered and real (10+ call sites in `public-booking-assistant.service.ts` alone) but this particular route resolves it through the customer-command pipeline's own classifier and intent handlers.

**Turn 1** — `"book me a neck massage with Gevorg on July 23rd at 1pm"` (fully explicit: service, provider, date, time). Result: hard `security_blocked` — `{"success":false,"action":"security_blocked","summary":"The customer assistant cannot perform \"create_booking\". Try rephrasing or use the booking menu."}"`. The LLM classifier guessed a plausible-sounding but non-existent action name (`create_booking`) instead of the real one (`book_appointment`), so the request never reached any booking logic at all — this is a distinct failure mode from mis-routing to a *different real* intent.

**Turn 2** — rephrased: `"please schedule me for a neck massage on July 23 at 1pm with Gevorg"`. Result: `success:true`, but classified to `check_providers_for_service` (a read-only availability lookup), not `book_appointment`. It correctly parsed everything — service (Neck Massage), date (23/07/2026), and even converted "1pm" Yerevan-local to the correct `09:00` UTC slot matching Gevorg's real availability — but merely listed that availability back, ending with `"Tap a provider below or reply with a name and time to book."` even though the prompt had already supplied both a provider name and a time.

**Turn 3** — literally following the assistant's own instruction: `"yes, book me with Gevorg at 09:00"`. Result: **regressed further** — `{"success":false,"action":"check_providers_for_service","summary":"Specify which service to check providers for.\n\nԱհա ինչպես ամragreլ ayc այս էջում. Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»։", ...}`. Two compounding bugs here:
1. The classifier again returned `check_providers_for_service` instead of `book_appointment`, despite an explicit "yes, book me" confirmation directly answering the assistant's own preceding question — the classifier never once produced `book_appointment` across all three turns of this conversation, no matter how explicit the phrasing became.
2. Within that (wrong) handler, service resolution itself failed: `handleCheckProvidersForServiceLogic` → `resolveService()` in [ai-payments.logic.ts:953-973](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-payments.logic.ts:953) (service lookup at [ai-payments.logic.ts:162-210](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-payments.logic.ts:162)) reads `params.serviceId`/`params.serviceName`/`params.serviceCategory` from the *current turn's extracted params only* — it has no fallback to the service already resolved and returned in Turn 2's response (`details.serviceId`/`serviceName` = Neck Massage). Because Turn 3's prompt mentions no service name at all (relying on conversation context, exactly as a real user would after the assistant already named the service twice), `resolveService` returns `undefined` and the handler fails with `"Specify which service to check providers for."` — actively losing context that was already established, not merely failing to advance.

**Secondary bug in the same response — a fresh, independent reproduction of the already-documented e2e-bug.87**: the guide text accompanying Turn 3's failure is corrupted, mixing Armenian script and Latin transliteration mid-word — `"Ահա ինչպես ամragreլ ayc այս էջում. Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»։"` — the exact same `"Yntreq masnaget kam «Vorqan eli hasaneli»"` string already quoted verbatim in e2e-bug.87's write-up. Root cause already isolated there, not re-derived here: the static, checked-in `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json` has its `step1`/`step2`/`step3` fields machine-translated into broken mixed Armenian/Latin/Cyrillic text across most blocks, while the parallel `.ru.json` file is clean for the same flows. This turn's `consumer-booking-flow` topic is simply one more affected block in that same file — not a new bug, but a 4th independent live confirmation (on yet another surface/flow) of how broadly e2e-bug.87 reaches: it now surfaces even mid-way through a failed AI booking attempt, not just on generic fallback/help responses.

**Turn 4 — abandoning pure natural language, tapping the AI-rendered availability button instead.** Turn 2's response included a real interactive card (provider name, role, 4 tappable time buttons) generated by the same `check_providers_for_service` handler — still part of the assistant widget's own rendered UI, not the manual booking flow. Tapping `09:00` under Gevorg Gasparyan navigated to `/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253/checkout?serviceId=...&startTime=2026-07-23T09:00:00.000Z&employeeId=...` — a **pre-filled standard checkout page**, i.e. the AI got the user to checkout correctly (service, provider, and time all carried through via query params), confirming the "stops at checkout" pattern documented everywhere else this session **is** what this specific handoff does by design here — it's a deep link into checkout, not a `book_appointment` call.

**Then a genuine end-to-end completion**: clicking the page's own "Հաստատել ամրագրումը" (Confirm booking) button **did fire `POST /public/:slug/bookings` → 201 Created**, producing a real, `confirmed`-status booking (id `0fd6939d-7368-48ae-aa59-80c4357511bf`, Neck Massage, Gevorg Gasparyan, 2026-07-23 09:00–09:50, customer Mary Torgomyan, $40, cash/pay-later). **This is the first time in this entire session's testing that an AI-initiated flow resulted in a real, completed booking** — but note the completion itself was a manual tap on the standard checkout form's own submit button, not an AI/chat action; the AI's contribution was narrowing the request down to a correctly pre-filled checkout link. **Test-data cleanup**: this booking was cancelled immediately after confirming it, via the account's "Իմ ամրագրումները" → "Չեղարկել ամրագրումը" flow (confirmed via UI: "This appointment is already cancelled." + `POST` to the manage-booking cancel endpoint) — no residual test data left behind.

**One confirm-click hiccup along the way, investigated and NOT counted as a bug**: my first click on Confirm (with a below-the-fold "Համաձայն եմ իմ տվյալների մշակմանը" / "I agree to my data processing" toggle still off) appeared to do nothing in that moment. Reading `checkout-form.tsx` afterward showed this is legitimate client-side validation, not a silent failure: `handleSubmit` (`checkout-form.tsx:413`) has an explicit `if (!form.consent) { setError(t('public.consentRequired')); return; }` at `checkout-form.tsx:433-436`, and `{error && <p className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</p>}` renders right after the consent toggles at `checkout-form.tsx:1063` — I simply hadn't scrolled back up from the fixed-position Confirm button to see it, so this is very likely a testing artifact, not a real defect. One genuine, minor, worth-noting UX inconsistency did surface while investigating, though: the Name/Email fields' labels bake in a visible `*` required-marker directly into their translated label text (`t('public.nameLabel')`/`t('public.emailLabel')`, rendered at `checkout-form.tsx:968`/`checkout-form.tsx:988`), but the equally-required consent `ToggleChoice` (`checkout-form.tsx:1029-1034`, label `t('public.privacyConsent')`) has no such marker — plus the validation error has no scroll-into-view behavior, so a user who taps a fixed-position Confirm button without noticing the page didn't navigate could plausibly miss the reason why. Not severe enough to warrant its own bug number, but worth a follow-up polish pass (add `*` to the consent label; scroll the error into view or show it near the fixed submit button).

**Verdict**: pure natural-language completion inside the chat never worked — across 3 turns of escalating explicitness (including a direct "yes, book me" confirmation echoing the assistant's own prompt), the classifier never once returned `book_appointment`, and the 3rd turn actively regressed, losing context already established two turns earlier. But the AI-rendered *interactive UI* (the tappable time-slot buttons inside the assistant's own availability card) **does** work end-to-end: tapping a slot deep-links into a correctly pre-filled manual checkout page, and completing that checkout (one more manual tap) produces a real, confirmed booking — confirmed live this pass with booking `0fd6939d-7368-48ae-aa59-80c4357511bf`, immediately cancelled afterward. So the accurate characterization is narrower than "never completes": **the AI can successfully hand off to a human-completed booking via its own generated UI, but cannot complete a booking purely through conversation, no matter how explicit or confirmatory the user's phrasing is.** Real-world impact: the "book via AI chat, hands-free" value proposition does not work on this surface — every real customer must still tap through at least one manual UI step (either the assistant's own slot button, or the full manual booking flow) to finish; the classifier's refusal to ever emit `book_appointment` from a conversational confirmation is the specific, fixable gap between today's behavior and true chat-driven booking.

**Fix direction**: (a) constrain/validate the classifier's action-name output against the real registered action list before dispatch (or map common hallucinated aliases like `create_booking` → `book_appointment`) instead of hard-blocking with `security_blocked`; (b) once a `check_providers_for_service` (or similar) response has already resolved a specific `serviceId`/`serviceName` into `details`, persist it into session/context state so a same-conversation follow-up like `resolveService()` (`ai-payments.logic.ts:162`) can fall back to it instead of demanding the customer repeat the service name; (c) add an explicit "book_appointment should be preferred once provider+time+service are all known, including from prior turns" rule to the classifier prompt/schema, mirroring the "Do NOT use check_providers_for_service" guardrail already present in the separate `PublicBookingAssistantService` schema (confirmed in `public-booking-assistant.schema.spec.ts:14-17`) — that guardrail exists on one pipeline but not this one; (d) the garbled-guide-text issue has no new fix direction beyond e2e-bug.87's own (re-translate `guide-flow-customer-public-i18n.hy.json`'s `step1`/`step2`/`step3` fields).

## consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 — Phase 1 (security-critical gap-fill): guest-token IDOR + public/customer boundary

Direct curl against the backend `/public/:slug/assistant` endpoint (same technique as the rest of this session), targeting the ~40 items left `- [ ] ... not tested this pass` in the plan's CLOSURE. This phase covers Section K (guest-token dedicated security pass) and Section L (public/customer surface boundary).

**e2e-bug.128 (CRITICAL) — `confirm_my_booking_details` never validates the guest manage-token at all; any garbage string plus a real `bookingId` leaks another customer's full booking details, unauthenticated.** — **Fixed:** (1) `resolveBookingForConfirmDetails` never queries by `bookingId` alone — signed-in path requires owning `customerId`, guest path requires a valid `manageToken` via `validateBookingManageToken`; (2) public assistant now forwards session `manageToken` into the handler; (3) invalid/missing token returns a generic manage-link clarify with no booking PII. Specs: `ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.spec.ts` (IDOR cases). Was: anonymous `bookingId` + garbage token returned full stranger booking details. Root cause: optional `...(customerId ? { customerId } : {})` dropped ownership for guests and never checked `manageToken`. Also closes **e2e-bug.96** (same IDOR).

**e2e-bug.128 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass on the single most severe finding of the session — confirmed genuinely fixed, held under a live exploit attempt.** Re-read `resolveBookingForConfirmDetails` (`ai-confirm-my-booking-details.logic.ts:105-177`): the guard is unchanged and structurally sound — when a `bookingId` is present, the code branches into exactly two paths, never a third that skips authorization: signed-in (`customerId` present) requires the booking row to match `{ id, businessId, customerId }` in the same `findOne` WHERE clause (not a post-hoc check that could be bypassed), and guest (no `customerId`) requires `manageToken` to be present *and* pass `validateBookingManageToken(booking, manageToken)` before the booking is ever returned — a missing or wrong token returns `{ booking: null }` with the booking row already dropped from scope, so no code path downstream can ever touch its fields. Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-confirm-my-booking-details'` — **3 suites passed (3), 93 tests passed (93)**, including the dedicated `describe('e2e-bug.128 / e2e-bug.96 guest manage-token IDOR')` block (6 tests: no-token, garbage-token, wrong-booking's-token, signed-in cross-customer attacker, legitimate guest-token success, and credentials-embedded-in-URL success).

**Live exploit attempt against the real running backend** (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`) using a real, existing stranger's booking (`3d1dc1da-...`, belonging to a genuine test customer "QA WA Guest", real service "Swedish massage", real appointment date) — the exact attack this bug describes, executed literally, with zero Authorization header in every request:
- `bookingId` in free text + no token at all → `{"success":false,"summary":"Share the manage link for this booking first, so I can look it up."}` — no service name, no date, no customer/employee name, nothing.
- `bookingId` threaded via `context.bookingId` (the realistic shape a shared/leaked URL would actually produce, matching how `e2e-bug.106`'s URL-query threading feeds this field) + no token → identical clean rejection.
- `bookingId` + an explicit 48-char garbage token (matching the real token's length/shape so it can't be dismissed as "obviously malformed") → identical clean rejection.
- **Positive control** (to confirm the fix isn't over-broad and hasn't accidentally broken legitimate guest access): same `bookingId` + the booking's *real* `manageToken` (read directly from the DB) → `{"success":true,"summary":"Your booking is confirmed for Swedish massage on 01/08/2026 09:00–10:00.",...,"details":{"serviceName":"Swedish massage",...}}` — full details correctly returned only when the real token is presented.

Three independent exploit shapes against real data, zero leakage in any of them, and a positive control proving the legitimate path still works exactly as intended. **Conclusion: e2e-bug.128 remains genuinely fixed** — this was the most severe finding of the entire testing session, and it holds under direct, repeated, live attack against real production-shaped data.
---

**Other Section K/L results, all clean:**
- **Mutating guest-token intents correctly validate tokens** (confirmed via source read above) — not independently re-verified live this pass to avoid mutating another customer's real test booking without cause, given the source-level proof already conclusively shows they route through `validateBookingManageToken()`.
- **No-session negative test (Section L, "higher priority")**: 3/3 clean. Anonymous requests for loyalty balance, subscription cancellation, and lab results all correctly demanded sign-in (`"Sign in to view your..."`) with zero data disclosed — this is the correct behavior the plan was checking for, and it holds even though the closely-related `confirm_my_booking_details` bug above does not.
- **Cross-tenant JWT test**: a session token minted for Business A's customer, sent against Business B's slug, returned a benign `"You have 0 loyalty points"` rather than an error or another business's data — not a leak, but also not a clean rejection; low-severity, informational only, not logged as a numbered bug.
- **`PUBLIC_ONLY_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS` parity spot-check**: 2/2 tested (`list_services`/`explain_business_hours_and_location`) behaved identically on the anonymous and signed-in endpoints — including identically reproducing the already-tracked e2e-bug.90 crash on `list_services` on both. Parity holds for what was checked; not exhaustively re-tested across all 14 given time.
- **Session-fallback-without-token test** (does the signed-in endpoint correctly use session bookings when no token is given): inconclusive — both attempts were misclassified by the LLM into unrelated actions (`explain_why_sign_in`, a hallucinated `list_upcoming_bookings`) before reaching the intended handler, consistent with the already-documented classifier-hallucination pattern rather than a new finding. Not pursued further this pass.

No test-data mutations occurred this phase (all requests were reads; the mutating guest-token intents were verified via source, not live-executed).

## consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 — Phase 2: compound/multi-step intents never tested this pass

7 compound intents driven live via curl against `gevgas-operations-7c299253`. Deferred to a follow-up pass, not covered this phase: `customer_clinic_compound`/`public_clinic_compound` and the intake/lab compounds (need `qa-test-clinic-cf58d2a9`, a different business), `tour_group_checkout`/`book_tour_nearest_departure` (need `qa-test-tours-aec5d941`), `public_service_rank_discovery_compound`, `guest_manage_visit` — cut for time after the pattern below became clear across a representative sample.

**e2e-bug.129 — `explain_my_subscription` is itself unreachable via natural language, which is why the `subscription_first_visit` compound can never get past step 1.** — **Fixed:** (1) `isOpenBillingSettingsPrompt` no longer treats bare "my plan" / visits-left as SaaS billing; (2) billing/loyalty rescue gated to `surface === 'dashboard'`; (3) `isExplainAiCapabilitiesPrompt` no longer matches bare "on my plan" without AI context; (4) provider `explain_package_visit_context` excludes customer "my plan" and client-context rescue gated to `surface === 'provider'`; (5) early customer/public `explain_my_subscription` rescue before meta-ops. Specs/eval: `ai-e2e129-explain-my-subscription.*`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E129_EXPLAIN_MY_SUBSCRIPTION_CASES`. Was: `"How many visits left on my plan?"` → `security_blocked` on hallucinated `summarize_my_appointments` / `open_billing_settings`. Root cause: dashboard billing, AI-quota, and provider package-visit detectors all matched "my plan" / "visits left" before CRM membership explain.

**e2e-bug.130 — a gift-card purchase request is severely cross-domain misclassified into multi-service-booking availability-checking, not any gift-card action at all.** — **Fixed:** (1) `isMultiServiceAvailabilityDiscoveryPrompt` / `extractServiceNamesFromPrompt` no longer treat "buy a gift card and check out" as multi-service (want+and split was inventing fake service names); (2) budget discovery maps purchase → `buy_gift_card` / `buy_gift_card_physical` / `buy_gift_card_for_someone` before `apply_gift_card_code` or `list_services` ($amount is face value, not maxPrice); (3) buy-* hints no longer set `paymentMethod=gift_card`. Specs/eval: `ai-e2e130-gift-card-purchase-vs-multi.*`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E130_GIFT_CARD_PURCHASE_CASES`. Was: `"I want to buy a $30 gift card and check out now"` → `check_multi_service_availability`. Root cause: multi-service discovery matched want+and; budget stole `$30` as maxPrice when rescue fell through.

**e2e-bug.130 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed.** Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='e2e130'` — **1 suite passed (1), 11 tests passed (11)**. `tsc --noEmit` surfaces 2 pre-existing type-narrowing errors in `ai-e2e130-gift-card-purchase-vs-multi.util.spec.ts:62-63` (`Property 'amount' does not exist` on a discriminated-union fixture type after a `.find()` lookup) — confirmed via `git status` that this spec file has zero uncommitted changes (it's clean at HEAD), so this is a pre-existing TS-strictness gap unrelated to this fix; it doesn't affect actual test execution (ts-jest still runs and passes all 11 tests) and is out of scope for this ticket.

**Live re-verification against the real running backend** (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`, signed-in `qa-web-single@example.com`):
- The exact original failing prompt, `"I want to buy a $30 gift card and check out now"` → `{"action":"buy_gift_card","summary":"Gift card $30 — total $30.00 (digital delivery).","navigate":{"path":"gift-cards/checkout","query":{"cardType":"monetary","amount":"30","deliveryMethod":"digital"}}}` — correctly classified and dispatched, with the real navigate payload confirmed live in the earlier gift-card-checkout regression work this session (`/gift-cards/checkout?cardType=monetary&amount=30&deliveryMethod=digital` renders correctly).
- A second, physical-delivery variant with a different dollar amount, `"I want to buy a 75 dollar physical gift card and check out now"` → `{"action":"buy_gift_card_physical","summary":"Gift card $75 — total $80.00 (physical delivery)."}` — also correctly classified, confirming the fix generalizes across both gift-card purchase variants and isn't overfit to the single `$30` fixture value.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.130 remains genuinely fixed** — the exact original repro and a second independent variant both correctly avoid the multi-service-availability misclassification and land on the intended gift-card purchase action.

**Reconfirmations of already-tracked bug families (not counted as new, but each is independent live evidence of broader impact):**
- `public_budget_service_discovery_compound` (exact fixture prompt, `ai-budget-discover-and-book-compound.fixtures.ts:14` — note this fixture's own `misclassifiedAction: 'create_booking'` field already anticipates a hallucination bug) → correctly decomposed to `check_providers_for_service` as step 1, but that step then failed with `"Specify which service to check providers for"` despite the prompt explicitly saying "haircut options under $50" — the same `resolveService()` category-filter gap documented in Section I (`ai-payments.logic.ts:162`), now shown to also break compound step 1, not just single-turn requests.
- `guest_book_and_manage` (anonymous, `"Book me the soonest available massage appointment and give me a link to manage it"`) → hallucinated `security_blocked: "cannot perform \"create_multi_service_booking\""`, another new hallucinated-action-name instance in the same family as `create_booking`.
- `guest_pay_cash_manage` (anonymous, `"Book me the soonest haircut, I will pay cash at the visit, and send me a manage link"`) → `compound_intent`, `"Stopped at step 1 (book_nearest_slot): Specify which service to book"`, despite "haircut" being named explicitly — same `resolveService`-family gap as above.
- `public_multi_service_compound` (`"I want a haircut and a massage together, whats available tomorrow"`) → `check_multi_service_availability`, `"Specify which services to check"`, despite both services being named explicitly — same gap, now confirmed to affect the plural/multi-service entity extractor too, not just the single-service one.

**Tested clean:**
- **Flexible-availability compound** (`"I want a massage Monday morning or Wednesday morning"`, an OR-window request) — worked correctly end-to-end: `check_providers_for_service` with two separate date/window sections in one response, each with real provider names and real time slots (Gevorg Gasparyan, 09:00–10:30 on both 20/07 and 22/07). Genuinely good multi-window handling; only the *named-service* extraction is broken elsewhere, not the *multi-window-date* logic.

**Pattern observed across this whole phase**: every compound that failed did so for one of exactly two reasons — either the classifier hallucinates a plausible-but-nonexistent action name (the `create_booking`/`create_multi_service_booking` family), or a correctly-classified step's own entity-extraction fails to pick up a service name the user stated in plain language (the `resolveService`/multi-service-extractor family, `ai-payments.logic.ts:162` and its plural sibling). No compound failed for a reason outside these two already-partially-documented families this pass — suggesting a fix to either one would have an outsized effect across many compounds at once, not just the single-turn cases already logged.

No test-data mutations this phase (all requests read-only or correctly stopped before any booking/purchase would have been created).

## consumer-ai-cmd-e2e-plan.1 — Phase 5 (FINAL): non-determinism / paraphrase-consistency check

Deliberately targeted 3 intents that tested fully clean earlier in this gap-fill pass (`explain_cancel_policy`, `explain_why_sign_in`, `loyalty_points_balance`) — testing paraphrase stability on already-broken intents would be uninformative, since they're already known not to work at all. Each intent sent 3 ways: formal, casual, and typo-laden. 9 requests total.

**e2e-bug.132 — `explain_cancel_policy` correctly classifies formal and even heavily-typo'd phrasing, but misclassifies the most natural, casual phrasing of the same question into a completely unrelated action.** — **Fixed:** (1) `isExplainCancelPolicyPrompt` matches casual "whats the deal if i cancel" / "what happens if I cancel" / typo cancelation rulz; (2) `hasPackageTargetCue` no longer treats bare "deal" as a package; cancel-without-package blocked from package-savings; (3) budget package-discovery no longer treats colloquial "deal if I cancel" as browse packages; (4) cancel-policy rescue runs before budget + package-savings steals. Specs/eval: `ai-e2e132-cancel-policy-casual.*`, `AI_COMMAND_EVAL_E2E132_CANCEL_POLICY_CASUAL_CASES`. Was: `"whats the deal if i cancel"` → `explain_package_savings` pricing list. Root cause: "deal" matched package-savings + budget discover_packages while cancel-policy required formal "policy/rules" wording.

**e2e-bug.132 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed.** Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='e2e132'` — **1 suite passed (1), 12 tests passed (12)**. `tsc --noEmit` clean for these files.

**Live re-verification against the real running backend** (`gevgas-operations-7c299253`, signed-in `qa-web-single@example.com`):
- The exact original failing prompt, `"whats the deal if i cancel"` → `explain_cancel_policy` with the real cancellation/reschedule policy text — no more `explain_package_savings` pricing-list steal.
- A second casual variant, `"what happens if I cancel"` → also correctly `explain_cancel_policy`.
- A heavily-typo'd variant, `"wat r ur cancelation rulz"` → also correctly `explain_cancel_policy`, confirming the original claim that typo-tolerance was never the weak point — casual/colloquial phrasing was.
- **Regression guard**: a genuine package-shopping question, `"whats the deal on your massage packages"` → correctly routed to `discover_packages` (the package catalog), confirming the fix didn't over-correct and swallow real "deal" + "package" questions into cancel-policy.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.132 remains genuinely fixed** — all 3 phrasing styles (formal, casual, typo-laden) now consistently reach `explain_cancel_policy`, and a genuine package-domain question with overlapping vocabulary ("deal") still correctly routes elsewhere.

**Milder related finding, same `explain_why_sign_in` intent**: action classification itself was stable across all 3 phrasings (formal/casual/typo-laden all landed on `explain_why_sign_in`), but only the formal phrasing (`"Could you explain the benefits of creating an account before booking?"`) actually got `success:true` with a real answer. Both `"why bother signing in"` and `"y do i need 2 sighn in"` — despite reaching the correct action — returned `success:false` with a generic clarification prompt (`"Ask whether you need an account, what signing in gives you, or how guest checkout compares."`) instead of just answering. Milder than e2e-bug.132 (the domain stayed correct), but still a real confidence/completeness gap that specifically penalizes casual and typo-laden phrasing — the two input styles a real mobile-app user is most likely to actually type.

**Tested fully clean: `loyalty_points_balance`.** All 3 phrasings — including the heavily-typo'd `"hw mny pnts i hav"` — correctly classified and returned the identical correct answer (`"You have 466.25 loyalty points (≈ $466.25 value)."`). Confirms classification robustness is intent-specific, not a uniform weakness — some intents (this one) hold up fine under paraphrase and typos, while others (`explain_cancel_policy`, `explain_why_sign_in`) degrade specifically on the input styles real users are most likely to produce.

No test-data mutations this phase.
