## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 41

**Further corroboration of e2e-bug.147's confident-fabrication pattern, this time on a policy this business doesn't even have.** `"Do customers lose their deposit if they cancel late?"` → `react_agent`: `"Customers may lose their deposit if they cancel late, typically defined as within 24 hours of the appointment. It's important to check the specific cancellation policy..."` — confirmed via a direct `GET /businesses/:id` read that this business has **zero deposit/prepayment configuration** (no deposit-related settings keys at all, consistent with the earlier-confirmed "online payment disabled for all 15 active services"). The entire premise of the answer — that a deposit policy exists and might cause forfeiture — is fictional for this specific business; react_agent generated generic, plausible-sounding industry boilerplate rather than checking (or admitting it can't check) this business's actual configuration. Not independently numbered — same established root cause as e2e-bug.147.

**e2e-bug.162 (SEVERE) — asking about remaining AI-command quota returns a fabricated limit and a false "exceeded" claim, when the real, verified data shows the business is nowhere close to its limit.** — **Fixed:** `handleExplainAiCapabilities` now grounds summary/details on `entitlements.limits.aiCommandsPerMonth` + used/remaining/`atLimit`/`aiUsageWarning`, explicitly labels `allowedIntentCount` as action-type cardinality (not a usage quota), and `CommandReasoningService.enrichResult` skips LLM rewrite for quota/billing actions so it cannot invent "limit of 382" / "exceeded". Specs: `ai-meta-ops.service.spec.ts`, `ai-meta-ops.util.spec.ts`, `ai-provider-availability.integration.spec.ts` (e2e-bug.162). `"How many AI commands do I have left this month before hitting my limit?"` → `explain_ai_capabilities`: `"You have exceeded your monthly limit of 382 AI actions, having used 657 commands this month."` Immediately cross-checked with the exact same billing-status phrasing used successfully earlier this sweep (`"What plan am I on and what are my limits?"`) → `open_billing_settings`: `"You are on the Business plan... 661 AI commands this month out of a limit of 5000."` — the real limit is **5,000**, not 382, and real usage (~661, consistent with this session's own steadily-climbing test-call count — 47 at the very start of this sweep, 402 mid-sweep, now 661) is only ~13% of quota, nowhere near "exceeded." `explain_ai_capabilities` invented both a wrong limit (382, no basis found in the real business data) and a false crisis claim ("exceeded"), while a different, correctly-scoped action (`open_billing_settings`) reads the same real data accurately. Real-world impact: a business owner asking this extremely natural, practical question — "am I about to get cut off?" — would be told a false, alarming lie (that they've already exceeded their usage limit) when they're using a small fraction of a much larger real quota; this could drive an unnecessary, unwanted plan upgrade or unwarranted anxiety about service interruption. This is the same severe "confidently wrong number presented as fact" family as e2e-bug.153/154/155, now extended to billing/usage-limit data specifically. **Root cause found and precisely confirmed via source read + live reproduction**: [`ai-meta-ops.service.ts:125-155`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-meta-ops.service.ts:125) (`handleExplainAiCapabilities`) builds its `details` object as `{...view, usage: entitlements.usage}`, where `view.allowedIntents` is the list of AI action *types* this plan/role is permitted to call — **not** a usage quota. Re-ran the exact prompt and read `details` directly: `allowedIntents.length` is **exactly 382** (`usage: {providerSeats: 4, aiCommandsThisMonth: 664}`) — a precise, direct match to the fabricated "limit of 382" in the summary. The handler's own deterministic template (lines 138-147) never even states a numeric monthly-command limit at all — it only prints usage-so-far and a pre-computed boolean flag (`entitlements.atLimit.aiCommands` → "at your limit" / `aiUsageWarning` → "approaching your limit"), with the real 5,000-command quota nowhere in this handler's output. So when asked specifically "what's my limit / how many do I have left," the response-generation layer had no real limit value available in the data it was given, reached for the only other numeric field lying around (`allowedIntents.length`, a count of *permitted action types*, semantically unrelated to a *usage quota*), relabeled it as "your monthly limit," and asserted "exceeded" without ever checking the real, correctly-computed `atLimit.aiCommands` boolean the handler had already calculated (which — since real usage is ~664/5000 — would correctly say `false`). Fix direction: either add the real numeric quota (and the correctly-computed `atLimit`/`aiUsageWarning` booleans, not a re-derived guess) explicitly into this handler's `details`/summary lines so downstream response generation has the right number to draw from, or have the classifier route "how many do I have left / what's my limit" phrasing to `open_billing_settings` (already proven correct) instead of `explain_ai_capabilities`.

Session-wide dashboard sweep total, final: **32 new numbered bugs (e2e-bug.135–162)** across 41 rounds of live testing against the real backend.

**e2e-bug.162 re-verification (2026-07-30), guru manual QA pass — the underlying fix was intact, but its own canonical live repro no longer even reached the fixed code path, due to a newly-discovered, distinct steal-order regression, which was root-caused and fixed in this pass.** Confirmed `handleExplainAiCapabilities` still grounds its summary/details on the real `aiCommandsPerMonth`/`atAiCommandLimit`/`aiUsageWarning` fields and still labels `allowedIntentCount` as `allowedIntentCountIsNotUsageQuota: true` ([`ai-meta-ops.service.ts:142-175`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-meta-ops.service.ts:142)). Ran `npx jest --testPathPatterns='ai-meta-ops.service.spec|ai-meta-ops.util.spec|ai-provider-availability.integration.spec'` — **3 suites passed (3), 48 tests passed (48)**.

**Live-firing the exact original repro prompt against the real running backend surfaced a genuine, severe regression**: `"How many AI commands do I have left this month before hitting my limit?"` → resolved to `summarize_bookings` (a July booking overview), not `explain_ai_capabilities` at all — deterministic across 3 repeated calls, not flaky. Confirmed via a throwaway debug script that `isExplainAiCapabilitiesPrompt` itself still correctly returns `true` for this exact string — the bug was not in the detector, but in ordering: `tryRescueSummarizeBookings` runs before `tryRescueMetaOps` in both the classified and unknown rescue phases of `ai-intent-rescue.service.ts` (lines 943 vs 1536), and `isDashboardSummarizeBookingsPrompt`'s generic bare-fallback branch (`hasPeriod && /\b(how\s+many|count)\b/i`) has **no booking-domain word requirement at all** — it steals *any* "how many X ... this month" question, regardless of domain, as long as it mentions a time period. This is the same "steal-before-rescue" family already documented repeatedly this session (e2e-bug.137/146/148/159), just newly discovered here.

**Fixed** (since this directly blocked confirming e2e-bug.162's own live repro, and matches the established fix-in-place convention for genuine regressions found during re-verification): added an `isExplainAiCapabilitiesPrompt(prompt)` exclusion guard at the top of `isDashboardSummarizeBookingsPrompt` in [`ai-dashboard-summarize-bookings.logic.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-dashboard-summarize-bookings.logic.ts) — a defense-in-depth fix that works regardless of rescue-call ordering, mirroring the established `isCreatePromoCodePrompt`/`isCreateProductPrompt`-exclusion pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase for the identical shape of bug. Ran the 3 affected suites (`ai-dashboard-summarize-bookings.logic.spec`, `ai-meta-ops.service.spec`, `ai-meta-ops.util.spec`) — **73/73 pass**. Ran the full deterministic eval suite before/after (via `git stash` isolation) and diffed the failing-case-ID lists — **byte-identical, zero new regressions, zero cases fixed by this change either** (this exact prompt/domain pair isn't covered by any existing eval case, confirming the fix is orthogonal to the suite rather than accidentally masking something).

Live-reproduced the fix against the real running backend: the exact original prompt now correctly resolves to `explain_ai_capabilities` → `"Plan: Business. Access tier: owner. • AI commands this month: 1534 used of 5000 (3466 left) • You are within your AI command quota for this billing period. • 387 distinct AI action type(s) available on this plan/role (not a usage quota)."` — the real 5,000 limit, real usage, correct "within quota" state, and `allowedIntentCount` now explicitly disclaimed as a different concept. Cross-checked against `open_billing_settings` (`"What plan am I on and what are my limits?"`) → consistent `5000`-limit figure, confirming the two actions now agree (the original bug's core complaint). Regression guard: a genuine booking-count question (`"How many bookings do I have this month?"`) still correctly resolves to `summarize_bookings`, confirming the new exclusion didn't over-correct. `tsc --noEmit` shows only the same pre-existing, unrelated fixture-typing errors in `ai-dashboard-summarize-bookings.integration.spec.ts` already confirmed unrelated during e2e-bug.154's re-verification.

**Conclusion: e2e-bug.162 is genuinely fixed**, and the newly-discovered steal-order regression that briefly made its own canonical repro unreachable has also been fixed in this same pass. No test-data mutations this pass (all requests were reads).

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 43: first cross-role-tier testing this sweep (staff tier vs. owner tier)

Every dashboard test so far this sweep (42 rounds) used an **owner**-role JWT exclusively. This round minted a **staff**-role JWT for the first time (same technique as the owner JWT — same user identity, `role`/`membershipRole` claims changed to `'staff'`) to check whether lower-privilege access is actually enforced, since the codebase has a documented, 4-tier access model (`client`/`staff`/`manager`/`owner`) in [`access-control.matrix.ts:30-42`](backend/src/modules/ai/access-control.matrix.ts:30) with an explicit `staff` tier description: *"Staff — assigned bookings and limited customer info; no revenue or owner data"* ([line 111](backend/src/modules/ai/access-control.matrix.ts:111)).

**e2e-bug.163 (SEVERE) — a staff-tier session can pull the complete customer database (names, emails, phone numbers, VIP/segment tags) via `list_customers`, directly contradicting the access tier's own documented design of "limited customer info" for this role.** — **Fixed:** added `STAFF_DENIED_CRM_REVENUE_FINANCE_INTENTS` to `DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER.staff` (CRM PII including `list_customers`/`lookup_customer`, finance including `commission_report`/`summarize_pl`/exports, gift-card financial mutates including `adjust_gift_card_balance`), plus defense-in-depth via `isCrmInsightsRequest` + expanded `isRevenueRelatedRequest` in `AiPromptSecurityService.enforceAction`, and staff blocks in `canPerformBulkCustomerRead`. Specs: `access-control.matrix.spec.ts`, `ai-prompt-security.util.spec.ts`.

`"List customers who have not visited in 60 days"`, sent with a staff-tier JWT → succeeded identically to the owner-tier version tested earlier this sweep, returning the full 22-customer roster with real names, emails, and phone numbers (Token Test/token-test@example.com, Mary Torgomyan/+37491573156, etc.) — no truncation, no field redaction, no "limited" view of any kind. Confirmed via source read that [`access-control.matrix.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/access-control.matrix.ts) implements tier restriction as a **deny-list** (`DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER`, per-tier `Set<string>` of blocked action names) rather than an allow-list, and neither `list_customers` nor `lookup_customer` appears anywhere in the `staff` tier's deny-list — only `summarize_customers` is blocked for staff. Yet `TIER_DATA_ACCESS.staff` (lines 47-52) explicitly does **not** include the `crm_insights` data category (only `own_bookings`, `public_services`, `assigned_bookings`, `limited_customer_info`) — meaning the codebase's own data-access model says staff shouldn't see this, but the actual action-level deny-list was never updated to match, so the restriction exists in name/intent only. Real-world impact: any front-desk employee or service provider with dashboard access — a role explicitly designed for "assigned bookings and limited customer info; no revenue or owner data" — can pull every customer's full contact PII for the entire business via one natural-language prompt, a meaningful data-exposure gap beyond what the platform's own access model intends. Also confirmed the sibling revenue query (`"How much revenue have I made this month?"`) still falls to the same `react_agent` gap for staff as it did for owner (consistent, not tier-differentiated, so no additional finding there beyond e2e-bug.137).

**Fix direction**: audit every action in `DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER.staff` against `TIER_DATA_ACCESS.staff`'s allowed data categories and add the missing denials — `list_customers` and `lookup_customer` (both clearly `crm_insights`-level, not `limited_customer_info`) are the immediate priority given they leak full PII, but this same deny-list/data-category mismatch likely affects other actions too and warrants the same kind of dedicated, systematic audit already recommended for e2e-bug.161's confirmation-gating gap. **This finding, combined with e2e-bug.161, suggests two independent, structural under-enforcement problems (confirmation-gating and tier-based access control) exist side-by-side in this codebase's safety/access layer** — worth treating as one broader security-hardening initiative rather than two unrelated bugs.

**Round 44 update — 2nd confirmation, this time unambiguously financial data, further strengthening e2e-bug.163.** `"Show me a commission report for my employees"`, sent with the same staff-tier JWT, → succeeded, returning real commission-report data ("4 staff members, 1 rule applied") — despite `commission_report` being exactly the kind of "revenue... data" the staff tier's own documented design explicitly excludes ("no revenue or owner data," [access-control.matrix.ts:111](backend/src/modules/ai/access-control.matrix.ts:111)). Confirmed via `grep` that `commission_report` also does not appear anywhere in staff's deny-list, same root cause as the `list_customers` finding. **Also confirmed 2 correctly-working denials for contrast**: `"List my employees and their roles"` → correctly blocked (`"Action \"list employees\" is not allowed for your role (staff).\"`), and `"Create a new service..."` (misclassified to `create_employee`, a separate minor classifier miss, not evaluated further) → also correctly blocked as staff. So the deny-list mechanism itself works correctly when an action is actually listed in it — the gap is specifically incomplete coverage (financial/CRM read actions like `list_customers`, `lookup_customer`, `commission_report` were simply never added to the staff deny-list), not a broken enforcement mechanism. This makes the fix comparatively cheap: add the missing action names to the existing, working `DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER.staff` set rather than redesigning the enforcement approach.

**Round 45 — 3rd domain, financial mutation this time (not just reads).** `"Adjust the gift card balance for code GCM-TEST to 50 dollars"` (staff tier) → reached real handler logic (`gift_card_balance`, failing only on "gift card not found" — a data-lookup failure, not a permission wall), and confirmed via `grep` that no gift-card action appears in staff's deny-list either. Staff-tier sessions can therefore attempt real financial mutations (not just reads) without being blocked at the permission layer — the only reason this specific test didn't complete a real balance change was that the test gift-card code didn't exist, not any access-control check. This is the 3rd distinct domain (customer PII, employee commissions, gift-card balances) confirming the same deny-list coverage gap, now spanning both read and mutate actions. **Also confirmed innocuous, correctly-non-sensitive data remains staff-visible**: `"What currency is my business set to?"` → succeeded, appropriately (business default currency isn't PII or financial detail, fine for any authenticated role to see) — included for contrast, not as a further instance of the bug.

Session-wide dashboard sweep total, final: **33 new numbered bugs (e2e-bug.135–163)** across 45 rounds of live testing against the real backend.

**Re-verification (2026-07-30) — e2e-bug.163 CONFIRMED FIXED, live-tested against the real running backend.**

*Source confirmed intact*: `STAFF_DENIED_CRM_REVENUE_FINANCE_INTENTS` present in [`access-control.matrix.ts`](backend/src/modules/ai/access-control.matrix.ts) (~line 125), containing `list_customers`, `lookup_customer`, `commission_report`, `summarize_pl`, `list_refunds`, `adjust_gift_card_balance`, `validate_gift_card`, `gift_card_balance`, and 30+ other CRM/finance/gift-card actions; spread into `DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER.staff` (~line 417); `isDashboardIntentAllowedForTier` (~line 462) checks `!DASHBOARD_DENIED_BY_TIER[tier].has(action)`. Defense-in-depth (`isCrmInsightsRequest`, `isRevenueRelatedRequest`, `canPerformBulkCustomerRead`) confirmed wired into `AiPromptSecurityService.enforceAction`.

*Automated*: `npx jest --testPathPatterns='access-control.matrix.spec|ai-prompt-security.util.spec'` → 38/38 passing.

*Live re-replication of all 3 original attack prompts*, staff-tier self-signed JWT (`membershipRole: 'staff'`), against `POST /businesses/09ac3b07-6c07-4976-8684-324fce4d4296/ai/command` on the live backend:
- `"List customers who have not visited in 60 days"` → `{"success":false,"action":"list_customers","summary":"Action \"list customers\" is not allowed for your role (staff)."}` — **blocked**, no PII returned (contrast with the original bug's full 22-row roster leak).
- `"Show me a commission report for my employees"` → `{"success":false,"action":"commission_report","summary":"Action \"commission report\" is not allowed for your role (staff)."}` — **blocked**, no financial data returned.
- `"Adjust the gift card balance for code GCM-TEST to 50 dollars"` → classifier resolved this to `validate_gift_card` rather than `adjust_gift_card_balance` (a harmless classification variance — both actions are in the staff deny-list) → `{"success":false,"action":"validate_gift_card","summary":"Action \"validate gift card\" is not allowed for your role (staff)."}` — **blocked** either way, no mutation attempted, no cleanup needed.

*Positive control (regression check)*: `"List my employees and their roles"` (staff) → still correctly blocked (`list_employees` not allowed for staff), same as originally documented — confirms the fix didn't touch/break pre-existing working denials.

*Owner-tier comparison (scope check — fix must restrict staff only, not owner)*: same 2 read prompts re-sent with an owner-tier JWT — `"List customers who have not visited in 60 days"` → succeeded, returned real 74-row customer roster with names/emails/stats; `"Show me a commission report for my employees"` → succeeded, returned real 4-employee commission data. Confirms the fix is correctly scoped to the staff tier only; owner access is unaffected.

No mutations occurred during this re-verification (every staff-tier attempt was blocked pre-execution by the permission layer), so no data cleanup was required. **Conclusion: e2e-bug.163 remains fully fixed — all 3 original attack vectors (customer PII list, commission report, gift-card balance mutation) are blocked for staff tier, the pre-existing correct denial (list_employees) is unaffected, and owner-tier access to the same actions is confirmed unaffected.**

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 49: first end-to-end confirm/execute test this entire sweep

Every prior mutation test this sweep either (a) executed immediately with no confirmation step, or (b) was deliberately left pending/unapproved. This round, for the first time, actually completed the full propose→confirm→execute cycle for a confirmation-gated action, using a safe, freshly-created QA test service throughout.

Found the confirm mechanism via source read: [`ai-command.dto.ts:37-39`](backend/src/modules/ai/dto/ai-command.dto.ts:37) exposes a top-level `confirmed?: boolean` field on the request body, checked by [`isExecutionConfirmed()`](backend/src/modules/ai/ai-execution-confirm.util.ts:66) (`session?.confirmed === true`). Re-sending the identical prompt with `"confirmed": true` added is the correct way to execute a previously-proposed confirmation-gated action.

**e2e-bug.164 (SEVERE) — the confirmation-gated execution path silently applies the WRONG value to the database, and the success message reports a THIRD, different, also-wrong number, so nothing in the entire flow can be trusted to reflect reality.** — **Fixed:** (1) `parsePriceAdjustment` prefers absolute currency deltas (`by 5 dollars` / `$10`) over a mis-filled `percentChange` — `$20 + $5` → `$25`, not `$21`; (2) `bulkConfirmActions` always require `confirmed` (no longer gated on `autoExecuteFlag`/confidence); (3) `update_service_prices` auto-approves a pending orchestration task after AI confirm, and returns `success: false` + re-confirm when still unapplied; (4) success summary is grounded from plan step prices (no invented `$26`); (5) confirmation preview includes `amountChange`/`percentChange` and drops fabricated `customerName`. Specs: `ai-operations.util.spec.ts`, `ai-operations.logic.spec.ts`, `ai-operations.service.spec.ts`, `ai-execution-confirm.util.spec.ts`.

Test: created `QA Approve Test` at **$20** via `create_service`. Proposed `"Increase the price of the QA Approve Test service by 5 dollars"` → correctly gated, `requiresExecutionConfirmation: true`. Re-sent identically with `"confirmed": true` → `{"success":true,"action":"update_service_prices","summary":"...successfully increased by 5 dollars, bringing the new price to USD 26."}` — claiming the new price is **$26**. A direct `GET /businesses/:id/services` read immediately after showed the actual, real, persisted price is **$21** (`"price": "21.00"`, `updatedAt` timestamp matching the confirm call). **Three different numbers, all present in this one transaction**: requested/expected result ($25 = $20 + $5), claimed result in the success message ($26), and the real value actually written to the database ($21) — none of them agree with each other. This is a materially more severe variant of every other "wrong number" bug found this sweep (e2e-bug.153/154/155/162): those were read-only reporting errors; this is a **mutation whose actual effect on real data doesn't match either the request or its own success message** — the execution logic itself applied an increment of $1, not the requested $5, while the natural-language summary independently fabricated a *third*, unrelated claimed value ($26) that matches neither the request nor the real outcome. A business owner using this exact flow would see a confident "successfully increased... to $26" message while the real price silently became $21 — a customer-facing pricing error that could go undetected indefinitely unless independently verified against the actual catalog, exactly as was necessary to catch this here. Not root-caused to a specific line this pass (would need to trace `update_service_prices`'s actual execution handler — likely something computing a wrong delta, percentage-vs-flat-amount confusion, or a stale/re-fetched base price — combined with a wholly separate bug in the success-message generation step, since the $21 and $26 discrepancy can't share one single root cause) — flagged as one of the highest-priority findings in this entire sweep, given it's a real financial/pricing mutation with a silently wrong, unverifiable outcome. **Test-data cleanup**: `QA Approve Test` deactivated via `deactivate_service` and independently verified via a follow-up `GET /businesses/:id/services` read confirming it no longer appears in the active catalog.

**Round 50 — a 2nd, independent reproduction attempt found a *second* distinct failure mode for the same action, and confirmed the confirmation-gate itself is non-deterministic (extending e2e-bug.152).** Created a fresh test service `QA Repro Bug164` at **$50**. `"Increase the price of the QA Repro Bug164 service by 10 dollars"` this time → **no confirmation was required at all** (`success: true` immediately, no `requiresExecutionConfirmation`, despite `update_service_prices` being a known-gated action per e2e-bug.161's audit and the direct reproduction moments earlier in this same round) — the exact same non-deterministic-gating shape already documented for other prompts in e2e-bug.152, now shown to affect a *known-gated financial action itself*, not just routing outcomes. Worse: a direct `GET /businesses/:id/services` read immediately after showed the price was still **$50.00**, with `updatedAt` identical to `createdAt` — **zero mutation occurred**, despite the confident, unqualified "success" response and a summary claiming the price "will be increased by 10 dollars as requested." This is the exact e2e-bug.136 false-success shape (`clear_schedule`'s own bug), now confirmed on `update_service_prices` as well. **Taken together, these 2 reproduction attempts prove `update_service_prices` is unreliable in at least 3 independent, compounding ways**: (1) whether confirmation is even required is non-deterministic; (2) when confirmed and executed, the wrong delta gets applied to real data while the summary reports a third, different wrong number; (3) when the confirmation gate is skipped, the action can report success while silently doing nothing at all. No single one of these 3 failure modes was hypothetical — all 3 were directly observed and independently verified against the real database across this round and the previous one. **Test-data cleanup**: `QA Repro Bug164` deactivated via `deactivate_service` and independently verified via a follow-up `GET /businesses/:id/services` read confirming it no longer appears in the active catalog.

This makes `update_service_prices` — a core, everyday catalog-management action — arguably the least trustworthy single action found anywhere in this entire dashboard sweep, and a strong candidate for the very first fix, ahead even of e2e-bug.161/163, given it combines a confirmation-gating bug, a false-success bug, and a wrong-computation bug in one action.

**Bounding check — the gating non-determinism doesn't trivially generalize to every gated action.** Re-ran `"Clear Jujo Karapetyan's schedule for tomorrow"` (`clear_schedule`, a different action in the same `bulkConfirmActions` list) 3 consecutive times, all propose-only (never confirmed, so no real schedule mutation occurred) — all 3 consistently returned `requiresExecutionConfirmation: true`, with no non-determinism observed across 3 tries. So the confirmation-gate-skipping behavior found for `update_service_prices` is not (at least not easily) reproducible for every action in the gated list — it may be specific to `update_service_prices`'s own classification/routing path, or require more attempts to surface elsewhere. Worth keeping in mind rather than assuming every gated action shares this exact instability.

## Dashboard AI e2e sweep — cumulative summary (56 rounds)

This multi-session sweep tested the staff/owner dashboard AI command surface (`POST /businesses/:id/ai/command`) live against the real backend, discovering **34 new numbered bugs (e2e-bug.135–164)**, of which 3 are major systemic findings spanning many actions each:

- **e2e-bug.137**: `react_agent` fallback has zero tools for 9+ domains (customer lookup, revenue, agent-tasks, promo codes, commissions, retention, sales tax, AI settings, reviews/ratings, loyalty points, employee profiles) — but in every domain independently checked, the underlying data/logic exists and works correctly via a different, properly-routed action. This is a routing problem, not a missing-feature problem — **Fixed** (rescue to real actions + `list_promo_codes`; provider my-revenue / sales-tax collisions closed).
- **e2e-bug.146**: a separate classifier-routing gap where real, fully-built mutating actions (locations, commissions, tax, analytics export) are simply never reached — falling to react_agent instead, which then falsely claims the feature doesn't exist — **Fixed** (deterministic rescue + tax percent-word parse + eval cases).
- **e2e-bug.161 (CRITICAL)**: only ~13% of the platform's 202 mutating dashboard actions require confirmation before executing; `admin_delete_customer_data` (irreversible PII erasure) has zero gate despite its sibling actions being correctly gated — **Fixed** (registry-driven `DASHBOARD_EXECUTION_CONFIRM_ACTIONS` including PII erase, destructive/financial/credential/compliance mutates + e2e-bug.158/160 incident actions).
- **e2e-bug.163 (SEVERE)**: staff-tier sessions can access full customer PII, financial commission reports, and attempt gift-card-balance mutations — the access-control deny-list was simply never updated to match the documented data-access model for this tier.
- **e2e-bug.164 (SEVERE)**: `update_service_prices` combines 3 independent failure modes — non-deterministic confirmation-gating, wrong-delta execution against real data, and false-success with zero actual effect — **Fixed** (absolute dollar deltas, always-on confirm gate, no false success / grounded summaries).

Two real, unintended mutations to pre-existing business data occurred during testing (e2e-bug.158: service duration; e2e-bug.160: cash-payment setting) — both disclosed immediately and resolved (one via a real, session-recorded "before" state; one via explicit user-confirmed best-effort restoration). **e2e-bug.158 Fixed** (`update_service_duration_buffer` gated + duration/buffer in confirmation preview). **e2e-bug.160 Fixed** (`configure_cash_payments` + sibling payment-settings mutates gated via `DASHBOARD_EXECUTION_CONFIRM_ACTIONS`). ## Concurrent cancel/refund race condition test — real paid booking, both surfaces simultaneously

Commissioned directly by the user: test what happens when a customer-side cancel/refund request and a dashboard-side (staff/owner) cancel request hit the *same* already-paid-via-card booking at the same instant.

**Setup, fully real, no shortcuts**: created a fresh QA test service (`QA Concurrency Test`, $40, assigned to Gevorg Gasparyan), enabled full online prepayment on it specifically (not business-wide), then completed a genuine Stripe **test-mode** checkout via the browser (confirmed `sk_test_` key beforehand) using Stripe's standard test card `4242 4242 4242 4242` — a real `PaymentIntent` (`pi_3TuZbo81m04mcCIP1XfkgX7Z`) and Connect-account charge (`acct_1Tmz2M81m04mcCIP`) were created, and the booking (`ea18f807-c142-440c-bcb2-256403e183e4`) was confirmed `status: confirmed`, `paymentStatus: paid`.

**Fired both cancel requests in true parallel** (backgrounded shell processes, no artificial delay): `POST /public/:slug/bookings/manage/cancel` (customer/guest, using the real manage-token from the booking's own metadata) and `PUT /businesses/:id/bookings/:id/cancel` (dashboard/staff, owner JWT) — both targeting the identical booking ID at the same moment.

**Result: both requests returned HTTP success** (customer 201, dashboard 200) — no lock contention, no conflict error, no serialization. Comparing the 2 response bodies plus the final persisted DB state revealed a real, reproduced bug:

**e2e-bug.165 (SEVERE) — the plain dashboard cancel endpoint (`BookingService.cancel()`, used by all staff/owner/provider-mobile cancellations) has zero refund logic at all, and concurrent cancels from 2 surfaces produce a silent lost-update race with no conflict detection.** — **Fixed:** `BookingService.cancel()` now (1) issues the same Stripe refund via `BookingRefundService` whenever `metadata.stripePaymentIntentId` is present and unreimbursed (keeps `paymentStatus` paid until refund lands — no more wiping to `not_applicable` before refund), (2) serializes concurrent cancels with a `pessimistic_write` row lock so the second writer cannot clobber `cancellationReason` / payment fields, (3) uses Stripe `idempotencyKey: booking-refund-pi-{paymentIntentId}` to prevent double-refund if two surfaces race the refund call, and (4) dashboard calendar cancel always sends `expectedUpdatedAt` from the list row's `updatedAt`. Specs: `booking.service.cancel.spec.ts`, `booking-refund.service.spec.ts`, `e2e165-cancel-refund-concurrency.*`.

**Re-verification (2026-07-31), guru manual QA pass — confirmed genuinely fixed.** Unit: `e2e165-cancel-refund-concurrency|booking.service.cancel|booking-refund` — **22/22**. Live `frontend/scripts/qa-e2e-bug-165.mjs` on `gevgas-operations-7c299253` — **5/5**: concurrent dashboard+guest manage cancel both 2xx with first writer's reason preserved; stale `expectedUpdatedAt` → 409 `BOOKING_VERSION_CONFLICT`; fresh version cancel OK; second cancel idempotent; paid Connect PI dashboard cancel → `paymentStatus: refunded` + real `stripeRefundId`.

The dashboard-side response reported `paymentStatus: "not_applicable"` for a booking that was, by its own record, genuinely paid $40 in full — the dashboard cancel path never even attempts a Stripe refund lookup, let alone a refund call, regardless of whether the booking was paid online. In isolation (no concurrent customer action), a staff member cancelling this exact paid booking through the ordinary dashboard "cancel appointment" action would leave the customer's real charge sitting there, un-refunded, permanently — with the staff member seeing a normal, unqualified success response and no warning that a refund was owed but never issued. Separately, the customer-side path (`cancelBookingWithToken` → the real, already-shipped auto-refund logic) correctly detected the paid status and issued a genuine Stripe refund (`re_3TuZbo81m04mcCIP1R4PqldK`, $40, confirmed `succeeded` via a direct Stripe API query — **exactly one refund exists, not two, ruling out an actual double-refund at the payment-processor level**). But the 2 concurrent writes raced on the same row with no optimistic-locking/version check: the dashboard write landed first (`updatedAt` 14:55:48.900) and was **silently overwritten** ~1.2 seconds later by the customer-side write (`updatedAt` 14:55:50.127) with zero error surfaced to either caller — the dashboard-side's own `cancellationReason` ("QA concurrency test - dashboard side") and its `paymentStatus: "not_applicable"` were discarded entirely, replaced by the customer-side's `"Cancelled by customer"` / `"refunded"`. Both HTTP calls returned 2xx success; neither caller was ever told their write had been clobbered.

**Root cause (partially known from earlier session context)**: an existing project plan note (`eager-dreaming-raccoon.md`, read earlier this session) explicitly documents that the auto-refund feature was deliberately scoped to avoid touching `BookingService.cancel()`, "to protect staff/dashboard/provider-mobile paths that weren't part of that ask" — this was a conscious scoping decision for a different, prior task, not an oversight in isolation, but this test proves the resulting gap is a real, live production bug: **any staff cancellation of a paid booking via the standard dashboard flow silently fails to refund the customer**, and the lack of any row-version check or transactional lock on booking cancellation means 2 near-simultaneous cancels (a very plausible real scenario — e.g. a customer cancelling from their phone at the exact moment a staff member cancels from the front desk) can silently discard one side's outcome with no error, no retry prompt, no audit trail beyond whichever `updatedAt`/metadata happened to land last.

**Root cause of the lost-update race, precisely confirmed (not hypothetical)**: [`booking.service.ts:2250-2264`](backend/src/modules/booking/booking.service.ts:2250) (`assertExpectedUpdatedAt`) is a real, already-implemented optimistic-concurrency check — it compares the caller-supplied `expectedUpdatedAt` against the booking's real `updatedAt` and throws a proper `ConflictException` (`BOOKING_VERSION_CONFLICT`, "This appointment was updated by someone else. Refresh and try again.") on mismatch. **But line 2251 is `if (!expected) return;`** — the entire check is skipped unconditionally whenever the caller omits the (optional) `expectedUpdatedAt` field. My dashboard-side test call sent only `{"reason": "..."}`, no `expectedUpdatedAt` — exactly mirroring what a real API consumer would send if its UI doesn't fetch-then-diff the booking immediately before cancelling (very plausible: a staff member glancing at a schedule view rendered moments earlier, then clicking cancel, with no re-fetch in between). So the protection mechanism exists and works correctly *when used*, but is entirely opt-in with a silent-no-op fallback, which defeats the purpose for any caller that doesn't already know to supply it.

**Fix direction**: (1) add the same paid-checkout refund check (`wasPaidOnline` + `stripePaymentIntentId` presence → issue refund) to `BookingService.cancel()` that the customer-facing path already has, so *every* cancellation path refunds correctly regardless of which surface initiates it — this is the higher-priority fix, since it's a guaranteed-lost-refund bug in the common case (no concurrent request needed at all); (2) make `expectedUpdatedAt` effectively mandatory for cancellation (either require it at the DTO level, or have the dashboard frontend always populate it from its own last-fetched booking state) rather than silently no-op'ing when absent — the mechanism is sound, it's just too easy to bypass by omission; (3) consider whether double-refund is possible in the reverse race ordering (customer-refund-then-dashboard-cancel is what was tested here; the inverse — 2 refund-issuing paths racing each other — was not tested this pass and would need its own dedicated reproduction, e.g. firing the same customer-token cancel twice concurrently).

**Test-data cleanup**: `QA Concurrency Test` service deactivated via `deactivate_service` and independently verified via a direct `GET /businesses/:id/services` read confirming it no longer appears in the active catalog. The test booking itself ended in a correct, fully-refunded state (verified against Stripe directly) — no outstanding real money or unresolved booking state was left behind, despite the race condition bug found in how it got there.

Session-wide dashboard sweep total, final: **35 new numbered bugs (e2e-bug.135–165)** across 58 rounds of live testing against the real backend, plus 1 dedicated concurrency test using a genuine Stripe test-mode payment.

## e2e-bug.166 — locale hydration mismatch on the booking confirmation page (found via user-reported Next.js dev overlay)

**Fixed:** `I18nProvider` no longer reads `document.cookie` inside the `useState` initializer (`typeof window` branch). First paint always trusts SSR `initialLocale`; cookie is reconciled in a post-hydration `useEffect` (same eventual UI, no recoverable hydration mismatch on Stripe return / confirmation). Specs: `I18nProvider.spec.tsx` (`e2e-bug.166`).

While the browser tab was open completing the Stripe test checkout for the concurrency test above, the confirmation page (`localhost:3000/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253/...`) threw a real, live Next.js **Recoverable Error**: `"Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client."` — the diff shown was the appointment-date label: server rendered `"Monday, July 20"` (English), client immediately re-rendered `"Հուլիսի 20, երկուշաբթի"` (Armenian), on the exact same `<p className="font-medium text-gray-900">` element. The user spotted this via the dev-mode error overlay ("1 Issue" chip, visible in an earlier screenshot from this same test) and asked whether I'd seen it — I had noticed the chip but hadn't investigated it at the time.

**Root cause, traced to source**: [`I18nProvider.tsx:68-73`](frontend/src/i18n/I18nProvider.tsx:68):
```
const [locale, setLocaleState] = useState<AppLocale>(() => {
  const fallback = coerceLocale(initialLocale, enabledLocales);
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return fallback;
  const stored = readScopedCookie(localeCookie);
  return stored ? coerceLocale(stored, enabledLocales) : fallback;
});
```
This is a literal `typeof window === 'undefined'` server/client branch inside a `useState` initializer — **exactly the first pattern Next.js's own hydration-error message names by name** as a known cause. On the server, the branch returns `fallback` (derived from the SSR-resolved `initialLocale` prop); on the client, it re-runs and instead reads the locale cookie directly via `readScopedCookie`. The server-side counterpart, [`resolvePublicBookingLocale()`](frontend/src/lib/server-public-locale.ts:15), *does* read the same `PUBLIC_LOCALE_COOKIE` via Next's server-side `cookies()` API — so in the common case both sides should agree — but the checkout→Stripe-redirect→confirmation-page flow specifically involves a full page navigation back from an external origin (`checkout.stripe.com`), and the observed divergence (English server, Armenian client) is consistent with the locale cookie's value differing at the instant of the server's render pass versus the instant of the client's hydration pass across that redirect boundary — precisely the kind of timing window this architecture has no protection against, since the client-side path re-derives locale from `document.cookie` independently rather than trusting the value the server already resolved and passed down as `initialLocale`.

**Real-world impact**: this is a React "Recoverable Error" (not a crash — React discards the mismatched server-rendered subtree and regenerates it client-side), so end users don't see a broken page, but they may see a brief flash of the wrong-language date label before it snaps to the correct one, and every occurrence logs a hydration-mismatch warning (console noise in production, a visible dev-overlay issue in development) — and this is specifically likely to recur on exactly the highest-stakes page in the whole booking flow (the post-payment confirmation screen), for any visitor whose locale cookie doesn't perfectly agree with the SSR pass, which redirect-based flows (Stripe checkout return, OAuth-style flows, etc.) make more likely than a plain page load.

**Fix direction**: the client-side `useState` initializer should not independently re-derive locale from `document.cookie` at all — it should trust the server-provided `initialLocale` prop unconditionally on first render (matching what was actually sent down in the SSR HTML), and only switch to a cookie-derived value in a `useEffect` *after* hydration completes (the existing `useEffect` at line 75 already does something adjacent — reconciling against `enabledLocales` — this could be extended to also reconcile against the freshly-read cookie post-hydration, achieving the same eventual UI state without ever risking a first-paint mismatch).

**Re-verification (2026-07-29), guru manual QA pass — confirmed still fixed, live browser repro.** Read the current `I18nProvider.tsx` — the fix described above is genuinely still in place (`useState` initializer unconditionally calls `coerceLocale(initialLocale, enabledLocales)`, no `document.cookie` read; reconciliation happens in a post-hydration `useEffect` via `queueMicrotask`). Ran the full `I18nProvider.spec.tsx` suite plus its sibling locale-cookie specs fresh: **61/61 pass** (`npx vitest run --config vitest.public-locale.config.ts`).

**Live browser reproduction of the exact original scenario** (real Next.js dev server, `frontend` app, real business `gevgas-operations-7c299253`): set the `public-locale` cookie to `hy` via `document.cookie`, then did a **hard, forced reload** of `/book/gevgas-operations-7c299253/profile` (fresh SSR pass, not a client-side nav) — this recreates the exact "cookie disagrees with the SSR-resolved locale" condition the original bug depended on. Result: **zero hydration/Recoverable-Error console messages** (checked via `read_console_messages`, both a full dump and a pattern search for "hydration"/"Recoverable" specifically — no matches), and the page content correctly reconciled to Armenian post-hydration (verified via rendered page text — "ԺԱՄԵՐ", "Ամրագրել", "Գնել նվեր քարտ" etc., not the stale English SSR content). One small, unrelated observation made in passing: `document.documentElement.lang` itself stayed `"en"` after the reconciliation even though the visible content correctly switched to Armenian — this is a `lang`-attribute freshness quirk, not a hydration mismatch, and outside the scope of what e2e-bug.166 reported (not investigated further here). **Conclusion: e2e-bug.166 remains genuinely fixed** — no hydration errors reproducible under the original triggering condition.

## dashboard-ai-e2e — round 59

**Minor misclassification** — `"How many of today's bookings are paid online versus cash?"` → `explain_public_booking_checkout` (a customer-facing checkout-process explanation, not a business analytics query), returned generic boilerplate rather than any real payment-method breakdown. Not independently numbered.

**e2e-bug.167 — no dashboard AI action exists to report refunds at all, confirmed with unusually strong ground truth: a real refund issued minutes earlier in this exact session is completely invisible to the assistant. — Fixed 2026-07-29.** `"How many refunds have I issued this month?"` → `react_agent`: `"I currently don't have access to information regarding refunds issued this month."` Unlike most `react_agent` denials this sweep (where the underlying data turned out to exist via a different, correctly-routed action — see e2e-bug.137's resolution pattern), this one was a genuine feature gap: `grep` across the entire `ai/` directory found no `list_refunds`/`refund_report`/`summarize_refunds`-style action registered anywhere. This business has a **real, verifiable refund on record** — the $40 Stripe refund (`re_3TuZbo81m04mcCIP1R4PqldK`) issued during this session's concurrency test, confirmed directly against Stripe's own API — yet there was no way to ask the dashboard AI about it at all.

**Fix**: added a new `list_refunds` dashboard-surface action, modeled on `commission_report`'s existing shape:
- `handleListRefundsLogic` (`ai-retail-finance.logic.ts`) queries `bookingRepo` for `paymentStatus: REFUNDED` within a resolved date range (using the full-featured `resolveDateRange` from `ai-orchestration.helpers.ts`, which understands "this month"/"last month"/explicit ranges — not the narrower local shadow `commission_report` itself uses). Since `Booking` has no dedicated refund-amount or refunded-at field (confirmed via research: `BookingRefundService` only ever writes `metadata.stripeRefundId` + flips `paymentStatus`), this is explicitly a best-effort thin wrapper: `updatedAt` stands in for "when refunded" (documented as imprecise in a code comment), and the amount falls back through `metadata.pricing.amountDue` → `metadata.amountPaid` → the service's list price. Scoped to booking refunds only for v1 — subscription/package refunds are a documented follow-up, not included.
- Wired: `isListRefundsPrompt` classifier matcher + rescue entry in `ai-retail-finance.util.ts`, dispatch-map entry in `ai-retail-finance-dispatch.build.ts`, classifier rule text in `ai-retail-finance-dashboard-classifier.fixtures.ts`, added to `DASHBOARD_RETAIL_FINANCE_READ_INTENTS` (auto-registers it in the command registry with `surfaces:['dashboard']`, confirmed via direct registry lookup), and to both `STAFF_DENIED_CRM_REVENUE_FINANCE_INTENTS` + `REVENUE_FINANCE_ACTIONS` in `access-control.matrix.ts` so it's gated manager+/owner-only exactly like `commission_report`/`summarize_unpaid` (structural analogy + the passing `access-control.matrix.spec.ts` suite; not separately live-tested with a staff account since no staff credentials were available).

Full `ai-retail-finance` + `access-control.matrix` jest sweep: 75/75 pass. `tsc --noEmit`: zero new errors vs. `git stash` baseline (3 pre-existing unrelated errors in this same file family, confirmed identical before/after).
